title: fix(post): post sinker side burns through explicit machine data
body:
## What changed

The shipped sinker post can post Sinker Side Burn with explicit machine data.
The machine must state `edm.codes.side` with `{x}`, `{y}`, `{z}`, and `{f}`.
The machine editor exposes this optional code role.
The post fills absolute endpoints in the work offset and converts coordinates and feed to the document units.
The downward entry still uses `edm.codes.depth`.
Each lateral feed uses the machine's `side` template.
The post refuses incomplete templates, incomplete coordinates, diagonal travel, changing lateral Z, invalid feed, and travel below program resolution.
Straight burns still need no lateral code.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3001-sinker-side-burn.md`.

## Cause

The post refused every Side Burn before the section opened.
Its feed handler supported downward Z burns only.
The generated Side Burn already states the plunge, lateral feed, return feed, and rapid retract.

## Tests

The first pin failed on unchanged production code at `f8a554045`.
It failed with the existing named Side Burn refusal.
The failure text remains outside the branch at `/tmp/3001-red.txt`.

The `script_sinker_side` suite passes all ten pins:

- `recorded_side_burn_posts_both_lateral_legs`
- `lateral_direction_and_amount_follow_each_recorded_axis`
- `lateral_endpoint_feed_and_electrode_reference_use_document_units_and_wcs`
- `straight_and_side_burns_post_together_to_recorded_nc`
- `side_burn_requires_explicit_complete_machine_dialect`
- `side_burn_refuses_diagonal_and_combined_vertical_lateral_moves`
- `side_burn_refuses_missing_or_non_numeric_start_and_end_coordinates`
- `side_burn_refuses_missing_zero_or_negative_feed`
- `side_burn_refuses_motion_below_the_program_resolution`
- `side_dialect_does_not_enable_lateral_moves_in_a_straight_burn`

The existing `script_sinker_iso` suite passes all 22 tests.
Its missing-dialect pin still refuses a Side Burn before any burn code.
The straight burn keeps its existing golden output.

Mutation checks:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Copy the original post from `upstream/main` back over the fixed script | Nine new pins fail. All ten pass after restoration. |
| Remove the required-placeholder guard | The complete-machine-dialect pin fails, then passes after restoration. |
| Remove the complete-coordinate guard | The missing-coordinate pin fails, then passes after restoration. |
| Remove the axis and constant-Z guard | The diagonal and combined-travel pin fails, then passes after restoration. |
| Remove the positive-feed guard | The invalid-feed pin fails, then passes after restoration. |
| Remove the formatted-zero-feed guard | The invalid-feed pin fails, then passes after restoration. |
| Remove the endpoint-resolution guard | The program-resolution pin fails, then passes after restoration. |

The gate ran on the final code with base `f8a554045`.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passes: 116 steps and 936 tests.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
No tests failed or were ignored in the quick gate.

## Goldens moved

One new file: `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/sinker-iso/sinker_side_burn.nc`.
The full diff was inspected.
Its 24 lines contain a straight burn, then a Side Burn plunge and both 0.15 mm lateral legs.
The lateral blocks use invented test codes from the synthetic dialect.
No existing NC or CL golden changes.

## Not exercised

No real EDM control or physical cut was exercised.
No real machine dialect was added.
The tests post the existing recorded CL fixtures through the shipped script.
The complete catalog workflow and manual machine editor interaction were not exercised.
No heavy lane ran.

## Overlaps

- #2893 touches `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` in the drilling cycle rows. This PR changes the sinker row.
- #2554 touches `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` in the `controller.post` section. This PR changes the EDM code roles.

Each touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
Neither changes the same lines or post functions.
No stack is required.

Effort: high

Process change: yes

Changelog: Sinker Side Burn posts explicit lateral feeds when the machine states a complete lateral servo template, with named refusals for unsupported data and unsafe moves.

Fixes #3001

title: fix(multiaxis): generate rotary contour rings about X
body:
## What changed

Rotary Contour generates rings around a cylindrical workpiece along X.
For a nearly horizontal axis, top and bottom specify axial ball-center stations.
Clearance and retract specify tool-tip radii about the fitted axis.
The planner reuses waterline contact geometry and radial links.
It refuses unsafe radii and invalid station bounds by name.
The decision record explains the parameter contract and alternatives.

## Cause

The station conversion divided world height by the fitted axis Z component.
An X axis has a zero Z component, so the generator refused it.
Removing that refusal alone would retain the invalid division and axial links.

## Tests

The initial geometry pin failed on unchanged upstream/main `97a880c53`.
The motion pins measure complete rings, axial bounds, radial poses, and link clearance:

- `rotary_contour_x_generates_complete_radial_rings`
- `rotary_contour_x_uses_the_translated_axis_for_clearance`
- `rotary_contour_x_refuses_clearance_inside_the_work_by_name`
- `rotary_contour_x_refuses_retract_inside_the_work_by_name`
- `rotary_contour_x_refuses_an_invalid_station_window_by_name`

All five pins failed with the original generator restored from upstream/main.
All five passed after the fixed generator was restored.
This mutation includes each new input guard.

The app pins passed on the real Tormach microARC machine definition:

- `rotary_contour_x_verifies_and_posts_finite_a_moves`
- `rotary_contour_x_in_oversized_stock_still_blocks_posting`

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 10 steps.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

## Goldens moved

None. The `.nc` and `.cl` diff is empty.

title: fix(import): read the STEP short name of the plane angle unit
body:
Stacked on #2927 (merge #2927 first).

## What changed

- The STEP model import expands two more ISO 10303-21 short names: `PLANUN` (`PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT`) and `GC` (`GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`).
- The `GUAC` and `SUNT` names of #2927 move into the same table, in the new module `crates/kernel/src/step_units_guard.rs`.
- A new check refuses a file by name when a plane angle unit cannot be converted to radians.
- The check also refuses a unit that measures a plane angle but is not marked as one. An angle is never read in a unit that the file does not state.
- New fixture `testdata/models/short_units_degree_cone.step`. It is our own 1 degree draft frustum (base radius 10 mm, height 10 mm), with short-name units.
- The STEP agreement bench gets a `Truck::NotRecorded` variant. #2790 removed the truck reader, so a new fixture has no truck reading. The bench must not make one up.

## Cause

The pinned p21 parser leaves `PLANUN` short. The solidcore-step unit reader then does not find the plane angle unit and uses radians. The cone semi-angle of 1 degree was read as 1 radian. With our fixture, the pcurve check then refused the solid with a misleading reason: "an edge lies 8.32 mm off the face's surface". A file whose edges do not hold the surface could pass with the wrong shape.

The short names come from the issue's reading of the public ISO short-name registry (`PLANUN` at line 1554). I could not fetch the registry again in this session.

## Tests

Pins (red before the fix):

- `step_short_units::short_name_degree_cone_keeps_its_angle`: volume and top radius of the 1 degree frustum. Before the fix: refused, "an edge lies 8.32039972978102 mm off the face's surface".
- `step_short_units::unmarked_angle_unit_is_refused_by_name`: the degree unit without its marker is refused, and the message names `#13`. Before the fix: the misleading pcurve refusal.
- `step_units_guard::tests::short_name_context_reads_degrees_and_uncertainty`: degrees and the `GC` uncertainty are read.
- `step_units_guard::tests::angle_unit_on_a_steradian_is_refused`.

Controls (green before and after): `long_name_degree_cone_control_keeps_its_angle`, `degree_unit_passes_the_angle_check`, and the five #2927 tests.

Mutation results:

- M1: remove the `PLANUN` mapping. The cone pin is red, and the check alone refuses the file by name ("unit #13 measures a plane angle but is not marked..."). Restored: green.
- M2: remove the `GC` mapping. The uncertainty unit test is red (`uncertainty: None`). Restored: green.
- M3: remove the `check_angle_units` call. The refusal pin is red. Restored: green.
- M4: skip the base-unit check. The steradian unit test is red. Restored: green.

Gates on the final code:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-2927` (the head of #2927): 82 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "kernel heavy"`: 16 steps, 0 failed (lib, bins, agreement, blend, heal_import, import_corpus, machining_mesh_shortfalls, mesh_deviation_bench, solidcraft_hostile, solidcraft_import, step_agreement, step_closed_form, step_import, step_short_units, step_twisted_flank, doc).

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes of `motion` and `app` were not run. They are reached only through the crate dependency graph (the `lib.rs` change). They must run before this PR is ready.
- The bench's raw tessellator (test-only `step_util::solidcore_mesh`) does not expand short names. #2919 recorded the same for lengths. Its pinned verdict for the new fixture is its refusal. The app meshes the record from `read_step`, which is correct.

## Overlaps

- #2927 changes the same rename step in `read_guarded` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs`). This PR is stacked on it.

Changelog: STEP import reads a plane angle unit given by its short name (PLANUN), and refuses by name an angle unit that it cannot read, so an angle in degrees is never read as radians.

Effort: high

Fixes #2973

title: fix(post): leave Agie jobs unarmed until the loaded work quality is verified
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review the [quality-binding correction above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018...ba5ff0ae123a87310a475692447f93a841d581a5).

A stale native quality can change the effective Ra, pass count and wire offsets while the controller formal check passes. A 40 mm Cobra trial bound the same 0.30 request to different existing records. The wrong selection ran three passes at 0.245, 0.165 and 0.140 mm. The intended selection ran four at 0.250, 0.170, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. A deliberately conflicting semantic name also defeated the returned handle and success-status checks after a new piece import.

CAMCraft now writes a complete native setup bundle and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. Geometry, start holes, work definitions and separation settings are present. The bundle records a stable quality name for the requested tuple and checks each assignment. The operator must review each effective native work in place before generating any machining steps. The operator can correct a mismatched quality without importing the piece again.

Check the actual wire, stock height, Ra, Tkm, Te and visible options in Work Details. For a mismatch, use Quality (Kwaliteit) and Define (Definiëren) on that same work. Confirm the requested values. Open Technology (Technologie), select TECCUT, and use Assign (Toewijzen) on the matching row. Check the individual working steps and their offsets before running GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK. The user guide gives the full procedure and the expected values for each supported setting. The native dialog exposes two of the three authored checkbox values.

On the deliberately polluted installation, a new import showed both works at [0]. FORMALCHECK reported a blocking technology error for each. Correcting Ra on the first work kept both at [0]. Explicit TECCUT assignment armed only the checked work. The installation retained the other unarmed work until its own review. The saved two-work piece then passed FORMALCHECK. GRAFICHECK produced 16 correctly ordered profile and separation blocks. All nine nominal faces had the verified 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm offsets. Both rough bridges measured 1.000 mm. The two cutting envelopes remained disjoint. The effective Ra 0.30 Berco process was checked independently at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 96 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. The app count includes machine, machine library and posting suites. It exported 20 jobs with 32 works. All 52 geometry and resource files matched previous output. Each of the 20 piece files changed from automatic machining to setup-only. Each repeat export preserved every file. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post, UI and geometry libraries. The final source revision reproduced all 72 files and reported working_steps_generated=false for all 20 jobs. The only change after that source revision is an operator guide sentence about the repeat-import result.

After manual release and plotting of both a mixed-radius Ra 0.30 piece and a rectangular Ra 0.35 piece, the tester reimported each exact SBL on its existing control. Each import created a new default-named piece with the intended ISO resource and zero steps. FORMALCHECK again reported technology undefined. The earlier named piece stayed separate. Select the newly created row and confirm its geometry and [0] before assigning the technology.

The real GUI status before the change reported the posted job. After the change it reports zero working steps, the requested targets, wire and stock values, and the required offsets. The two UI screenshots were checked locally. Public screenshot attachment is pending.

Effort: high
Changelog: Agie native jobs import with zero machining steps. Review each work's effective native quality and offsets before assigning its technology in Agie Control.

Fixes #2984

title: fix(app): judge the first traverse of a 3+2 plane against the machine table
body:
Stacked on #2985 (merge #2985 first). This PR has one commit of its own on top of the #2985 head `73e10f954`: `7e6e2ffe3`.

## What changed

- The first-traverse law (#2985) now reads the machine table on a 3+2 plane. Before, it skipped the table in each tilted frame.
- The law reads the table's top face over the stated X/Y travel. The table box is clipped to the Z travel, which starts at the table top. The 1e6 mm slab under the top face is out of the tool's reach.
- The law reads the table only when the head can tilt. The machine file states which rotaries turn the work (`turns_part`, #804). When each tilting rotary turns the work, the table stays under the work, and the law does not read the table.
- A mounted machine that states no X, Y and Z travel has no table box. A 3+2 plane on such a machine gets a note: "First traverse: the machine table is not judged on this tilted plane: ...". It is not a silent pass.
- Files: `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` (the predicate `work_tilts`, the clip `table_top_face`, the note), and `generate.rs` (passes the rotary list, adds the note to the path).
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2987-table-tilted-first-traverse.md`.

## Cause

- #2985 skipped the table in a tilted frame. A full read of the table box refused each indexed operation on the microARC 4.
- I measured why. A read of the top face alone still refused them: Z 190.5 at A 90 and Z 336.55 at A 180. Those refusals are false. The microARC 4 turns the work, so its table never stands over the plane.
- On a head-tilt machine the table is fixed in the world. The tilted plane drops toward it on its low side. That collision passed.

## Tests

New file `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table.rs`. It uses a small test machine (X and Y travel +-100 mm, Z travel 0..300 mm) with three rigs: head tilt, work tilt, and head tilt with no travel.

- `a_head_tilt_plane_under_the_table_inside_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`: B 30 deg, plane 20 mm over the origin, table top face at 32.68 mm along the axis. The verdict is `FirstTraverseLow { fixture: true }` and the post is refused by name. **Red before the fix.**
- `a_head_tilt_machine_with_no_travel_names_the_table_unjudged`: the note is on the path. **Red before the fix.**
- `a_head_tilt_past_90_reads_the_table_top_face_not_its_slab`: B 120 deg. A plane 100 mm over the origin passes, and a plane 90 mm over it is refused at the top face (96.6 mm).

title: fix(import): the STEP edge-gap cap follows the tolerance that the file states
body:
## What changed

- **Edge cap** (`crates/kernel/src/step_edge_gap.rs`, new). An edge may lie off its face's surface by up to `clamp(2 x stated, 0.01 mm, 0.02 mm)`.
  - `stated` is the distance uncertainty of the file. Solidcore's units module reads it and converts it to mm, so an inch file converts. When there are several contexts, the least value is used.
  - A file that states no uncertainty, or zero, a negative value, NaN or infinity, keeps 0.01 mm (`MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM`).
  - No file can raise the cap past `EDGE_GAP_LIMIT_MM` = 0.02 mm.
  - `KernelTrims::with_cap` applies the cap to the gap check and to the pcurve lift check.
- **Refusal text** names the gap, the cap and the source of the cap. Example: `edge 0 lies 0.0210 mm off the face's surface, over the cap of 0.02 mm; the file states a tolerance of 0.01 mm, and the reader accepts twice that, from 0.01 mm to 0.02 mm`. The start of the old text is the same, so the pins of `bspline_discontinuous.step` (0.25 mm) did not change.
- **Looser mesh** (`crates/geometry/src/step.rs`). The importer meshes the model one more time at `min(2 x stated, 0.02 mm)` when all of these are true:
  - the machining mesh refuses at the chord (`FaceCapped`, `EdgeCapped` or `Deviation`);
  - the file states a tolerance;
  - a kept edge gap is larger than the chord.

  The importer hands out that chord. Thus the existing #864 law (`step::coarse` -> `coarse_mm` -> `ReducedFidelity` -> `model_fidelity`) flags the model. There is no second derivation of the fidelity law, and no schema or project-file change.
- **Notes.**
  - The importer note, in plain words. The geometry crate gives the facts, and the app adds what the fidelity law does at that chord (`geometry::import::step::loosened_consequence`, which reads the same law as `verdict_tol`). At 0.02 mm the note is: "This file's edges sit up to 0.018 mm off their surfaces. The file states a tolerance of 0.010 mm. The model is used at reduced accuracy (0.020 mm). A program cannot be posted while this model is in the document. Export the file again with a tighter tolerance to post one."
  - When the excess is inside `DEV_TOL`, the second part is: "Gouge checks against this model are stricter, and an operation that they cannot check is refused at the post."
  - The kernel note for each kept gap over 0.01 mm names the gap, the stated tolerance and the cap.
- **Advice texts for a coarse model (review fix).** The document does not record why a model has reduced accuracy. Issue #2996 adds that record; then each text names the one cause. Until then six texts name both remedies ("re-import with a larger STEP facet budget, or export the file again with a tighter tolerance"):
  - `model_fidelity::TOO_COARSE`;
  - the MCP note (`model_fidelity::facts`);
  - the `op_problem` refusal of a kind that cannot read the excess;
  - the vouch refusal of a recorded chord (`commands/vouch_fidelity.rs`);
  - the model-page hint (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`). This is a text change only; the page layout does not change, so there are no screenshots;
  - the `import_model` MCP tool description.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2976-edge-gap-cap.md` (the maintainer chose option A on 2026-11-20).

## Measurement (local harness, not committed; cap off for the run)

| File | Stated (mm) | Edges measured | Largest gap (mm) | > 0.001 | > 0.005 | > 0.01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lobe.step (private user file) | 0.01 | 28 | 1.015e-2 | 14 | 10 | 1 |
| fig8.step | 0.01 | 1 | 3.5e-12 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| fillet_corner.step | 1e-6 | 2 | 8.2e-13 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| bar_cross_holes.step | 2e-5 | 4 | 1.19e-6 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| bspline_discontinuous.step | 1e-6 | 3 | 0.25 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| the other 16 tracked models | 1e-14 to 0.01 | 0 | - | - | - | - |

`Lobe.step` with this PR (local run, numbers only): it imports. Chord 0.02 mm, 10640 facets, deviation 1.947e-2 mm. The mesh volume is 113192.5 mm3, and the exact kernel volume is 113295.5 mm3. It has the reduced-accuracy note ("up to 0.010 mm ... states a tolerance of 0.010 mm ... reduced accuracy (0.020 mm)"). The numbers are the same after the merge of `main` with #2934 (strip-face division in the mesher). At the chords 0.005 to 0.015 mm, the mesh refuses one face ("face 1 capped", sag up to 1.56e-2 mm).

## Cost (read this before the merge)

- 0.02 mm is coarser than the verdict tolerance of the stock simulation (`DEV_TOL` = 0.01 mm). A gouge of less than about 0.02 mm on such a model is not judged. The flag and the note tell the user.
- At a chord of 0.02 mm, the excess over `CHORD_CAP` is 0.015 mm. That is more than `DEV_TOL`, so `model_fidelity::verdict_tol` has no tolerance left.
- The program gate (`op_problem`) refuses an operation on such a model by name when the floor of the operation does not cover the excess. `VouchModelFidelity` does not apply to a recorded chord.
- `gate_problems` adds the `verdict_tol` refusal when no operation is refused by itself. Thus the post refuses each program while such a model is in the document, also when each operation leaves stock that covers the excess.

## Posting waits for #2996

The maintainer decided to widen the verdict tolerance for such a model in a follow-up. Until then, on a model that opens at 0.02 mm, the user can:
- open the model, see it, measure it, and set up stock and fixtures;
- make and generate operations (the gate names each operation that it cannot verify);
- read the reduced-fidelity flag and the note.

The user cannot post a program while this model is in the document. Refs #2996

## Pins (our own generated fixtures, `testdata/models/edge_gap/`; provenance in each header)

- `crates/kernel/tests/step_edge_gap.rs` (6 tests):
  - a gap of 0.018 mm with a stated 0.01 mm reads with the note, and the mesh refuses at 0.005 mm but meshes at 0.02 mm;
  - 0.021 mm is refused with the new text;
  - a stated 5 mm does not raise the cap past 0.02 mm, and the 0.021 mm step is refused by the mesh;
  - with no stated value, the cap stays 0.01 mm (0.009 mm reads at the kernel, 0.011 mm is refused by name);
  - the inch file converts (0.0003 in gives a cap of 0.01524 mm; 0.014 mm reads, 0.016 mm is refused);
  - `fig8`, `fillet_corner`, `bar_cross_holes` and `twisted_flank` keep tight gaps and no looser mesh.
- `crates/kernel/src/step_edge_gap.rs` unit tests (3): the clamp, NaN and limits, the refusal text, the loose-chord rule and the note text.
- `crates/geometry/tests/step_edge_gap.rs` (4 tests):
  - 0.018 mm meshes at a chord of 0.02 mm with the note first;
  - the inch file meshes at 0.01524 mm;
  - the file with no stated value (0.009 mm) and the file that states 5 mm are refused at the chord;
  - the over-cap files and `bspline_discontinuous` are refused at the cap;
  - the four tracked fixtures keep the chord of 0.005 mm.
- `crates/app/tests/import_step_edge_gap.rs` (2 tests):
  - `ImportModel` carries `coarse_mm = 0.02` and the full note, and `chord_of` after execute is 0.02;
  - the over-cap file is refused;
  - the four tracked fixtures keep `coarse_mm` `None`;
  - (third test) both branches of `loosened_consequence` (0.02, 0.01524, 0.012).
- Texts of the advice: the full new text in app `model_fidelity`, `coarse_laws`, `coarse_rims`, `fidelity_copies`; new asserts for the MCP note (`model_fidelity`), the vouch refusal (`vouch_fidelity`), and the page hint (ui `model_fidelity`, `model_incomplete`).
- Unchanged and green: `step_twisted_flank` (kernel, geometry, app), `import_step_guard_default_cap`, `import_step_guard`, and every kernel `step_agreement` row.

## Gate (head 7b2dba40d, after the merge of `main`; -j 18)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --locked --no-fail-fast`: 22 binaries, 119 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
- Geometry `step_csys_read`, `step_diag`, `step_edge_gap`, `step_metre_unit`, `step_twisted_flank`, `step_units`: 28 passed, 0 failed.
- App `import`, `import_bytes`, `import_outward`, `import_solidcraft`, `import_step_*` (12), `model_fidelity`, `step_chord_units`, `step_fidelity`, `vouch_fidelity`, `vouch_fidelity_mcp`, `stock_copy_hole`, `coarse_laws`, `coarse_rims`, `fidelity_copies`, `step_budget`, `pocket3d_hsm`: 26 binaries, 125 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored.
- `camcraft-ui` lib (from `crates/ui`): 1319 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy subset in release (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --only ...`, 21 steps, 16.4 min, 0 failed):
  - every kernel heavy step (lib, bins, agreement, blend, heal_import, import_corpus, machining_mesh_shortfalls, mesh_deviation_bench, solidcraft_hostile, solidcraft_import, step_agreement, step_closed_form, step_edge_gap, step_import, step_twisted_flank, doc);
  - app `adaptive_fig8_crossing`, `import_solidcraft`, `large_models`;
  - the two known fails of #2845 (red as expected).
- The other heavy steps (`cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` lists 249 in all) go to the cut gate.

## Not exercised

- **Heavy lanes:** only the STEP, mesh, import and fidelity subset above ran. The other heavy steps go to the cut gate.
- The new fixtures are in `testdata/models/edge_gap/`, not at the top level. The `step_agreement` bench needs a recorded truck reading for each top-level fixture. The truck reader was removed in #2790, and a row with an invented reading would be false.
- A file that states a large tolerance does not reach the kernel's gap check: the reader fits those pcurves itself. Such a file is not meshed looser. The mesh refuses it by name at the chord.
- A file with no stated tolerance and a gap between 0.005 mm and 0.01 mm passes the edge check. The mesh refuses it at the chord, as before.
- No GUI run. The page shows the existing reduced-fidelity label, and the hint text changed (pinned in the ui tests).

Test build: from 364e4b4f4 (see the PR comment). The maintainer tested that build by hand. The review fixes and the merge of `main` came after it.

Effort: max (no escalation). Refs #917

Changelog: STEP import: the cap on how far an edge may lie off its surface now follows the tolerance that the file states (twice it, from 0.01 mm to 0.02 mm). A model whose edges stop the mesh at the normal accuracy is imported at reduced fidelity, with a note that names the gap and the file's tolerance.

Fixes #2976

title: feat(wire): post convex tangent DXF line and arc contours on Agie
body:
**Apply the quality-binding correction in #2984 before machine use or merge.** The following measurements describe the geometry on the tested control.

Stacked on #2992. Review the [convex tangent DXF changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/c81cfd1d44c0c210d5ba8ddc0fb1a63c3ac81342...feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018).

Use one complete, placed convex DXF loop of tangent lines and circular arcs as a Wire Contour punch. Keep the actual directed source segments. Check the emitted arc radii, tangencies, support line and complete stock envelope. A bounded, conservative preview runs through the normal workspace verification. The native writer keeps the nominal centers and arc sweeps.

The operator selects the placed profile, supplies an exterior threading point, and selects the supported captured punch process. Require a long enough supporting straight side for the entry and 1 mm separation. Folded, discontinuous or ill-conditioned loops and a rounding change that invalidates native tangency refuse before publication.

Run the original examples:

```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/rounded-punch.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/three-corner-punch.camscript
```

Agie Control plotted the first job with four true corner arcs and alternating nominal radii of 4 and 6 mm. Their rough radii were 4.245 and 6.245 mm. The second job used three true circular sweeps of about 143.1301, 126.8699 and 90 degrees, plus an oblique straight side. Both jobs retained the 1.000 mm nominal separation. Each formal check had zero job errors and requested reference and machining setup. The control reported option 131072. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 34 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post and geometry libraries. The integrated branch reproduced both three-file jobs byte for byte. See #2984 for the separate safety correction to the binding of a resident quality.

Effort: high
Changelog: The Agie post preserves the nominal lines and arcs of a checked convex tangent DXF punch, including unequal corner radii and oblique sides.

Refs #2022

title: feat(ui): draw the viewport overlay as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA
body: ## What changed The viewport overlay drew as `wgpu` lines. A `wgpu` line is always 1 hardware pixel and has no anti-aliasing. Toolpaths, height planes, outlines, triads and the ground grid now draw as wide anti-aliased lines. The viewport also has MSAA. - **Wide lines** (`crates/ui/src/viewport/wide.rs`): - Each segment is one 32-byte instance: two f32x3 points and two RGBA8 colours. The grid fades along a line, thus each end keeps its own colour. - The vertex shader makes a quad that faces the screen. The fragment shader fades the sides and the ends over 1 px. - The old 1 px `LineList` overlay pipeline is removed. - **Clean corners.** Each end reaches half the line width past its point. Two lines that meet close the corner and do not overlap past it. - **Depth lift.** Each vertex moves toward the eye by 3 line widths (`LIFT_WIDTHS`). The world size of one pixel comes from the `mvp` matrix, so the lift is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection. - The lift prevents this: without it, the depth test hid half of a line that lies on a face. - Effect: a line behind a face by less than 3 line widths shows through. This is a few pixels of depth on the screen. - **Near plane.** The shader clips a segment to the near plane before it calculates the screen direction. Thus an end behind the eye does not turn the quad over. - **Line width setting.** The choices are 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 pt. The default is 1.5 pt. The value is multiplied by the display's pixels per point, and the result is held to 1..16 px. - **Anti-aliasing setting.** The choices are Off, 2x and 4x. The default is 4x. - All viewport pipelines and the traced-stock composite use the same sample count. - A change rebuilds the pipelines and the multisample and depth targets one time. The resolved colour target stays, so the egui texture stays bound. - The traced stock writes one depth for each pixel. Thus its own edges are not smoothed, and its cost does not change. - **Sample counts that the device offers.** - Bring-up requests `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` when the adapter has it. The shell then reads the adapter's counts for the colour and depth formats. - Without the feature, only WebGPU's guaranteed counts 1 and 4 are offered. The browser build offers 1 and 4. - A row for a count that the device does not offer is disabled, and its hover text gives the reason. A queued pick of such a count is refused by name. - A kept count that the device does not offer falls back to the highest offered count below it. The status line says so one time. - **Where the settings are.** - They are in the Theme door, under "Colour vision", as the groups "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing". - They are kept in the per-user `view.json` (`app::view`), with the origin-name switch. A file word that the build does not know reads as the default and does not refuse the file. - They are not on the undo history and do not make the document unsaved, the same as the theme. - The origin-name switch now writes all the view settings, so it does not reset the line settings. - **File size.** The pipelines and the render targets moved to `viewport/pipes.rs` and are built through one helper. `viewport.rs` went from 1543 to 1265 lines. - **Docs.** - The guide has a short paragraph in "Themes and screen readers" (`first-run.md`). - The decision record is `docs/decisions/2958-wide-overlay-lines.md`. ## Screenshots Before and after: 1 px lines without anti-aliasing (`main`), and 1.5 pt lines with 4x anti-aliasing (this PR, the defaults). The Theme door with the new "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing" groups: The line widths: 1 pt with anti-aliasing Off, 1.5 pt with 4x (the default), and 3 pt with 4x: ## Readings Frame time: a 2560×1440 target, a release build and DX12, the median of 35 frames (submit and wait). The scene is one plate and a raster path at the overlay limit (512k segments), or a typical path (20k segments). "Before" is `main` at acd5b02d3 (1 px lines, no MSAA). "After" is 1.5 px wide lines. | GPU | Path | Before (1 px) | After, Off | After, 2x | After, 4x | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 20k segments | 0.17 ms | 0.20 ms | 0.26 ms | 0.29 ms | | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 512k segments | 0.27 ms | 0.70 ms | 0.72 ms | 0.78 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 20k segments | 1.00 ms | 1.33 ms | 3.38 ms | 3.64 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 512k segments | 1.77 ms | 6.92 ms | 8.76 ms | 9.09 ms | On the integrated GPU, the cost is clear: - 4x adds approximately 2.3 ms to a typical frame at 1440p. - At the overlay limit, the frame is 9 ms. This is near the 10 ms frame target. The default 4x follows the issue. If the maintainer prefers the lower cost on integrated graphics, the default can change to 2x or Off. This is a one-word change (`Antialias::default`). - Upload (`set_overlay`) of 512k segments: 9.6 ms (NVIDIA) and 8.8 ms (AMD), against 7.1 ms and 7.0 ms before. The upload occurs only when the scene changes, not when the camera moves. - Overlay buffer at the limit: 16 MiB (32 bytes for each segment). Before, it was 24 MiB (two 24-byte vertices). - Without the lift, the pinning test counts 292 px of a 6 px line on a face against 628 px in the air. With the lift, the two counts are the same. ## Pinning tests - `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render/wide_lines.rs` (in the `gpu_render` binary): - `a_line_on_a_face_keeps_its_full_width`: fails without the lift (292 vs 628 px). - `two_lines_that_meet_close_the_corner_and_do_not_reach_past_it`. - `the_line_width_setting_widens_the_band`. - `msaa_smooths_the_edges_that_one_sample_leaves_hard`. - `crates/ui/tests/trace_composite.rs`: `the_traced_stock_paints_the_same_with_msaa`. The 4x pass with the composite has no validation error. - `crates/ui/src/viewport/wide_tests.rs`: - `each_segment_is_one_32_byte_instance` - `an_odd_vertex_and_bad_colours_never_reach_the_gpu_as_garbage` - `the_line_width_scales_with_the_display_and_stays_in_range` - `an_unoffered_sample_count_falls_back_to_the_highest_offered_below_it` - `the_shader_lifts_by_the_documented_widths` - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/theme_door_quality.rs`: - `the_defaults_are_one_and_a_half_points_and_four_samples` - `a_line_width_pick_is_kept_survives_a_restart_and_undo_leaves_it` - `an_offered_antialias_pick_is_kept_and_an_unoffered_one_is_a_disabled_row` - `a_queued_pick_of_an_unoffered_count_is_refused_by_name_and_not_kept` - `crates/app/tests/view_file.rs`: `the_line_width_and_the_antialias_round_trip`. ## Gates - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on 0cd1a634f: 22 steps, 0 failed (2.6 min). - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on 0cd1a634f: the change in `app::view` reaches all the `app` heavy lanes. 201 steps ran in 34.3 min, and 200 are green. The 7 known-fail markers are red as expected. - One step is red: `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (got `(3158, 3130, 1141)`). title: fix(cl): the opening rapid starts over its entry point; the clearance plane must clear the stock and the fixtures
body:
## What changed

1. **Seat (from the held commit `edd41f0f5`).** The opening rapid of a clearance-seeded milling path starts over its own entry X/Y on the clearance plane (`cl::Toolpath::seat_approach(seed)`). It does not start at the WCS origin (#2382's seat, reversed) or at the frame zero. The end of the rapid does not change, so no posted block changes.
2. **First-traverse law (new).** After a tool change the machine does not know its X/Y. The post sends Z to the clearance plane and then X/Y at that plane, so that traverse can cross any point of the setup. The new law `sim::verify::first_traverse_low` gives the blocking verdict `Warning::FirstTraverseLow { at, height_mm, top_mm, fixture }`. The start height of the path must be at or above the top of the start stock and the top of each fixture, in the frame of the operation.
   - The stock top is the full start stock, not the in-process stock.
   - A 3+2 plane reads the eight corners of each box along its tool axis. It does not read the machine table slab (`MAX_FIXTURE_DIM` wide): along a tilted axis that slab gives a "top" of about 1e6 mm. Upright frames read the table. The first traverse of a 3+2 operation against the machine table is thus not judged: #2987 (P1) owns that gap.
   - Scope: 2D milling, 3D milling and vertical hole kinds on a mill without a rotary axis, upright or 3+2. The rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds have no such law yet: #2965 (P1).
   - The rule is in `camcraft-sim` (it owns `Warning` and `FixtureBox`). `app` passes the extents in `operation/first_traverse.rs`. `generate.rs` gets two calls. MCP names the verdict `first_traverse_low`. No new crate dependency.
   - Reuse check: no existing law blocks this case on every path. `RapidInStock` needs a known line. The "Clearance in stock:" note does not block. The `grblhal` and `tinyg` posts refuse only for the stock, and only in those two posts.
3. **Words.** The door word at creation and the "Clearance in stock:" note no longer offer "face the stock first" as the fix (a face does not lift the first traverse over the start stock).
4. **Cache.** The op stamp salt changes from `v3` to `v4`. Old caches read Stale once.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2901-first-traverse-law.md`.

## Site and guide (review round 1)

- `site/tests/test_guide_images.py` pins the regenerated counts: `Indexed Face1` `{gouge: 30, first_traverse_low: 1}`, `Swarf1` `shank_hit: 884` (was 897).
- `site/content/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md` names the first-traverse-low warning and says what it means and how to fix it. `site/content/guide/multi-axis/operations-multiaxis.md` states 884 shank hits.
- `site/content/guide/reference/troubleshooting.md` no longer tells the user to face the stock first for a clearance plane inside the stock. It has a new entry for the first-traverse message: its text, its meaning and its fix.

## Readings

- WCS at the stock corner and at the stock centre (`wcs_start`): Face1, Finish1 and Drill1 give the same moves for the two WCS positions. The opening rapid has no X/Y travel and starts on the clearance plane over the entry. No move reaches the world origin. The first posted X/Y block is the entry less G54.
- Before: the opening rapid of Face1 started at the G54 corner (40, 20) at Z 30 and travelled to the entry. After: it starts and ends over the entry.

## Refusal texts

- Stock: `Op1Contour: the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z8.000, under the stock top at Z10.000 - raise the clearance height above Z10.000`
- Fixture: `Face1: the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z30.000, under the fixture top at Z40.000 - raise the clearance height above Z40.000`

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/first_traverse.rs` (new):
  - `a_far_clamp_over_the_clearance_plane_holds_the_post_by_name`
  - `the_same_clamp_under_the_clearance_plane_posts` (the control: the program is byte-identical to the program with no clamp)
  - `a_3_2_plane_reads_the_stock_top_along_its_tool_axis` (B 10 deg: refused at Z 25, posts at Z 30)
  - `the_simulation_opens_over_the_entry_on_the_clearance_plane`
- The stock case (Z 8 under Z 10): `stale_rapid_law::regenerating_the_old_cache_judges_it_under_the_new_law`.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/first_traverse.rs`: 4 unit tests (stock, far fixture, at-or-above passes, tilted corners).
- The pins of `edd41f0f5` stay green: `wcs_start` (6), `origin_approach` (8).

## Changed test expectations and goldens

No expectation is weaker. Details are in the decision file.

- `stale_rapid_law`: `RapidInStock { at: 0 }` -> `FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm: 8.0, top_mm: 10.0, fixture: false }`, and the refusal must name the op and both heights. The same program is refused at the same move for the same cause.
- `clearance_in_stock`: 4 cases name the new verdict in place of `RapidInStock { at: 0 }`. One case reverses (the known cost): `the_same_plane_over_stock_an_earlier_face_cut_down_is_air_and_posts` -> `..._holds_only_for_the_first_traverse`. The traverses inside the path are still acquitted by the face ahead, but the first traverse holds the post. The door word now says "raise Clearance to the stock top or above".
- `wcs_start` clamp test (held work): the 40 mm clamp on the old origin-to-entry line gets no struck-move verdict and no routed link. Only the first-traverse verdict holds the post.
- `operations` (slot helper): the Z 5 plane in a 20 mm block is now the first-traverse verdict, not the "Clearance in stock" note.
- `stock_source_holes` framed B 10 deg chamfer: the clearance changes from 25 to 30. The tilted block's corner is at 25.77 along the tool axis.
- `center_cut_owed`: the expected facer path gets the same seat.
- `stock_play`, UI `sim_readout_names_the_op_and_the_verb`: the zero-length opening segment takes no time.
- `regression_models` minutes: `0.35983333 -> 0.35933333` and `1.47475343 -> 1.46766667` (no opening travel from the frame zero).
- `deburr_cache_stamp`, `wire_stamp`: stamp pins recaptured under salt v4.
- CL goldens, only the `START` line changes. Each new value is the end of the opening rapid:
  - `circular_ramp_stay_down`
  - `contour_start_point`
  - `pocket_waterline_square_dogbone`
  - `pocket3d_trochoidal_pocket`
  - `pocket_rest_corners`
  - `pocket_adaptive_v63` (read with `include_str!`; I edited this one line by hand)
  - `thread_mill_external_m10_single_form`
  - `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form`
- **No NC golden changes.**

## Example projects (regenerated, `.nc` byte-identical)

These projects were loaded, then each operation was regenerated with `GenerateOperation` and the project was saved with `project::save`:
- `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`
- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`
- `examples/first-router-part.camproj`
- `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj` (by the maintainer's answer)

The diff is the stamps, the start of the opening rapid, the file version and the tool `number` fields. In `guide-multiaxis`, the Swarf1 cache also moves by one rounding step in 402 coordinates, and its shank-hit list follows the current law (897 -> 884; the changed moves are 639-1010, inside the path).

The committed `.nc` files do not change (`git diff` shows no `.nc` file). The continuous test's `WRITE_GOLDEN` path would rewrite 7 A-words by one last digit, so I did not use it.

The two operations of `guide-multiaxis` were blocked before (gouges, shank hits) and stay blocked. Indexed Face1 also gets the first-traverse verdict.

## Known cost

An operation whose clearance plane is under the stock top or a fixture top on purpose is refused, for example a contour after a face took the whole top down. The message says to raise the clearance height.

In the tests this law changed 9 tests in 5 files, all fixtures inside `crates/*/tests`. Only one of them went from "posts" to "refused". No catalog case and no shipped `.nc` stopped posting.

## Gate

- The quick gate falls back to batch (`crates/cl` changed).
- One full pass on `6ae9b6a77`: debug builds plus the cl, motion, sim, post, app and ui suites, 929 steps, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=18`. 926 steps passed. The 3 red steps (4 failing tests) are fixed in `806aa0cf9`.
- On `806aa0cf9`, after `git merge origin/main`, these passed:
  - `catalog_groove_part_off`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_edge_work`
  - `first_traverse`, `stale_rapid_law`, `wcs_start`, `stock_play`, `wire_stamp`
  - `first_4axis_part`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_router_part`
  - `golden_cl`, `fixture_route`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `clearance_in_stock`, `operations`, `center_cut_owed`, `regression_models`, `stock_source_holes`, `thread_boss`, `solid_law_goldens`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `deburr_cache_stamp`, `pocket_no_adaptive`, `rest_pocket`, `pocket3d_trochoid`, `circular_stay_down`, `contour_start_point`, `corner_relief`
  - `camcraft-cl` `origin_approach`, the `camcraft-sim` lib tests, and the `camcraft-ui` lib tests (1290 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The site tests ran with Python only (`python -m unittest discover -s site/tests`). The Zola build tests need `zola` on `PATH` and did not run. The other red site tests (`test_guide_icons` act-report icon, `test_first_4axis_part` and `test_first_continuous_4axis_part` bold-label checks, and the Zola errors) are red on `origin/main` too.
- Known: `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs` is 471 lines (it was 460, already over 400).
- Known: `stock_play::the_transport_maps_onto_the_plan_by_name` accepts either opening outcome. A stricter pin needs a build; the coordinator schedules it.

- The release heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run.
- The full batch did not run on the final head after the second merge of main. The coordinator runs it.
- No machine run.

Changelog: The opening rapid of a milling operation now starts over its own entry point instead of the WCS origin. The program is refused by name when the clearance plane is not above the stock top and every fixture top, because the first rapid after a tool change comes from an unknown X/Y. Saved toolpaths regenerate once.

Effort: max (escalated from high)

**Apply the quality-binding correction in #2984 before machine use or merge.** The two-work geometry and clearance measurements describe the tested resident process. Every work also needs the intended effective quality.

Stacked on #2979. Review the [paired die changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/e9676b0df6d4b4463d9fbd56789e3ca6e2333232...f53d50d77c7b06ed2407cedfa9c16627f8655f43).

Check both threading holes, both captures, all cut envelopes and all work references before publishing any file. The group uses the common 20 mm resident QN2 process. Its SBL requests a quality tuple. Check the effective quality in the control editor.

Run the synthetic job with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/die-pair.camscript`. It creates the DUODI20 resource and piece files and a separate ISO file for each opening. Each opening on the 120 by 60 mm retained plate generated 41 moves with zero warnings.

The actual Agie Control applied inward offsets of 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm to all 76 faces. It roughed both openings, cut the two 1.000 mm separations, then ran three trims on each opening. The ten cut blocks stayed in two disjoint areas. The control made no cutting move across the retained plate. The formal check reported zero job errors. The control requested manual setup and reported option 131072 at both works. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 25 scoped app tests, 17 native post tests and strict Clippy for the app, geometry and post libraries. The final integrated branch reproduced all four controller-tested files byte for byte.

title: feat(wire): post placed DXF racetracks and circles with native Agie arcs
body:
Stacked on #2974. Review the [placed DXF wire changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/760e62cc194f49d6efb51cfd557574d7df4cede0...80daeae0852e3f46a6ebfa5b47c13aeb2689b592).

Use one closed DXF racetrack or circle as the source for a vertical punch. Keep the original lines and arcs through placement, normal Wire Contour generation, verification and native output. Invalidate the toolpath when the source or placement changes. The conservative preview encloses the exact arcs with at most 0.000025 mm of radial excess.

A racetrack needs two parallel cardinal straight sides tangent to two semicircles. A circle needs a radius from 6 through 15 mm and a radial threading lead on a cardinal side. The native grid must represent the circle and the intended seam. Individual chain selection, other drawings and laser work remain part of #2022.

Run the original examples from the repository root:

```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/racetrack.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/circle-punch.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/north-circle.camscript
```

The translated and 90 degree rotated R10 racetrack generated 1,409 moves with zero warnings. Agie Control kept the arc centers at (−6, 1) and (10, 1). It reported pass radii of 10.245, 10.155, 10.140 and 10.134 mm. The arc direction reversed on alternate passes. The separation on the straight section measured 1.000 mm.

On circular jobs, each bridge swept 1/R radians for a 1.000 mm nominal arc. The rough and trim wire paths stayed concentric. Three CAMCraft jobs exercised R6 east, R10 west and R15 north. Separate synthetic reference jobs checked all four cardinal directions at R10. The formal checks reported zero job errors. The control requested machining and reference setup and reported option 131072. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 24 scoped app tests, 15 native post tests and both round-profile geometry tests. Strict Clippy passed for the app, geometry and post libraries. In the integrated feature branch, all 13 example jobs and three additional stock heights exported correctly. All 50 files matched their earlier verified output. Each repeat export preserved every file.

Effort: high
Changelog: Placed DXF racetracks and circles can drive a verified Wire Contour punch and produce native Agie arcs from the original drawing.

This first cutoff process uses 20 mm stock.

cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/cutoff-upper.camscript

At a nominal Y of −6, the left cut measured Y −5.755, −5.845, −5.860 and −5.866 mm. The right cut gave the mirrored values about positive Y 6. All other cutting moves stayed in air. Both formal checks had zero job errors. The control requested machining and reference setup and reported option 131072. No physical cut was made.

## What changed

Each catalog case has separate `regenerates` and `rebuilds` tests.
The five cases now have ten independent workflow results.
The suite has 16 tests, up from five. No test is ignored.
Each workflow has a 60-second wall-clock budget.
Each workflow prints its name, elapsed time, and budget, including when it fails.
Shared assertions move to a helper module. Both source files stay below 400 lines.
Each rebuild removes only its own scratch directory.
The existing NC comparisons and portability checks remain in place.

## Cause

Two loops ran all cases inside two tests.
The first failed assertion stopped each loop.
The tests did not measure or limit each case.

## Tests

Pins:

- `contract::every_case_has_two_named_test_results` checks both workflow names for every discovered case.
- `contract::two_broken_cases_report_both_names_and_times` checks two named failures and their times in each workflow.
- `support::a_case_over_its_budget_fails_by_name` checks a named timeout and its heavy-lane guidance.

The first two pins failed on unchanged upstream/main `61a817bed` before the fix.
Both pass with the fix.
The budget pin passes with a 1 ms limit and a 50 ms worker.

Mutation checks:

- Restoring the original file and retaining the contract pins makes both pins fail. Restoring the fix makes both pass.
- Replacing `recv_timeout` with unbounded `recv` makes the budget pin fail. Restoring the timeout makes it pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passes all 16 tests.
All ten workflows run in debug mode. Their times range from 0.256 to 12.415 seconds in the gate.
The first full debug run took at most 21.617 seconds for a case.
All cases stay below the budget, so none moves to the heavy lane.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

The release heavy lanes, UI, and a real machine did not run.
A real hanging model did not run. The timeout pin uses a sleeping worker.
The timeout bounds the test result. It cannot cancel the worker thread.

#2913 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
It adds `slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor` and its helper.

title: feat(wire): post a native Agie Classic Cut 2S job
body:
**Hold for the quality-binding correction in PR #2999 for #2984 before machine use or merge.** A preexisting controller quality with the same generic name can select a different target, pass count and wire offset. The original tests establish the plotted geometry on the tested control. They do not establish the requested quality on another installation.

Stacked on #2948. The parent is a fork branch. This draft targets upstream main. Review the [native writer changes above the machine template](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/08601a2bc50abcbe2e550c86d3f9e708cbd49071...83affaca1bf4920ed07e29bf7c52bf9c48561b80).

## Change

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust and selects resident control technology. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This draft retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

The offline Classic Cut 2S control imported a CamCraft-generated 40 by 20 mm punch. Its formal check reported zero errors. It reported warnings for setup, reference values and selected option 131072. Its graphical check plotted the rough pass and three trims outside the nominal punch. Their straight-face offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. The first passes skipped a 1 mm segment. A later sequence cut that segment and returned to the threading hole at X-30 Y0. The simulated stock extended from Z0 to Z-20. No physical machine cut was made.

The synthetic example runs from the repository root:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
```
Use a new PUNCH40 destination.

## Final head checks

At head 83affaca1, all nine native application integration tests passed. The tests include the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch, qn2_requires_the_rough_wire_size_in_the_mounted_condition and the_work_must_fit_between_each_stated_guide. The ordinary command script generated three files identical byte for byte to the earlier offline control input.

The unconfigured machine, absent or wrong condition role, missing wire diameter, and missing or unsupported separation each produced a diagnostic and no output directory. Independent verification passed 93 scoped checks: 81 app integration tests, four native writer tests, one geometry test, six existing Post dialog tests and one actual desktop Post button check. Both GUI and CLI output matched all three controller input files byte for byte. Strict all-targets Clippy passed on camcraft-app, camcraft-post, camcraft-geometry and camcraft-ui.

The quick planner selected a 983-step workspace batch. The heavy planner selected 248 steps. Only the plans ran for those full gates. This PR remains a draft.

## Desktop Post dialog

| Before (Generic ISO) | After (native Agie) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic ISO Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/625ef345a047980ab6974df99ea8ca2ac5f783b2/before.png) | ![Native Agie Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/625ef345a047980ab6974df99ea8ca2ac5f783b2/after.png) |

Effort: high
Changelog: The Wire EDM desktop and script workflows can post a supported Classic Cut 2S punch as a native Agie job directory.

Fixes #2945

Add the AGIECUT Classic 2S wire EDM machine template to the desktop and embedded machine libraries. Mounting the template preserves the selected post.

The template states the X/Y rapid speed of 900 mm/min, the Z/U/V rapid speed of 600 mm/min and U/V travel of ±70 mm. It lists the four standard wire sizes from 0.20 to 0.33 mm. The X/Y/Z stroke lengths appear in the description. The operator supplies the installed datum, guide planes and cutting conditions. The handbook qualifies its maximum taper angle by guide type and work height.

The native job post is separate work in #2945. This change does not select an Agie dialect.

## Source

[AGIE, AGIECUT Classic technical handbook, edition 06.2002 C2.1](https://static.gindumac.com/products/9ccc9b7e-b589-49db-9843-eff1da09434c/documents/ES-EDM-AGI-2002-00001.pdf). Section 1.1 on printed page 4 identifies the model group, travels and speeds. Section 5.2 on printed page 44 lists the wire sizes.

## Verification

Independent checks used head 08601a2bc. All 68 tests in machine, machine_library, mcp_wire_contour and posting passed. Clippy passed on all camcraft-app targets with warnings denied.

The pinning tests are:
- agiecut_classic_2s_exposes_the_sourced_axes_and_wire_sizes
- agiecut_template_refuses_a_wire_job_without_an_installed_condition
- every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration

The normal command script selected the exact library name and mounted AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S. An attempted wire job with C110 failed with a missing-condition diagnostic. It created no NC file. Physical travel and cutting were not tested.

title: ci(gate): batch lanes for separate runners (--lane N/M) and gate-verdict
body:
This PR is the `xtask` part of #2908. It does not change `post-merge.yml`. The issue stays open for the workflow.

## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate batch --lane N/M` runs lane N of M of the batch plan (new module `xtask/src/lane_split.rs`).
  - The split is a round-robin deal in plan order. It reads no timing file. Thus each runner computes the same lanes for the same commit.
  - Each test step and clippy is in exactly one lane. The steps that share the machine are dealt first, then the steps that run alone (`lanes::ISOLATED`, ui, clippy).
  - A lane keeps the `debug build: <crate>` step of each crate that it tests.
  - `--lane 1/1` is the full batch plan of today.
  - The batch plan of this repository has 973 steps. Three lanes get 325, 324 and 324 steps.
- A lane run writes `lane-result.tsv` into its `gate-logs/batch-<stamp>/` (new module `xtask/src/verdict.rs`). The record has the lane, the runner name (`RUNNER_NAME`), the result, the wall time, the planned step count and one row for each step that ran.
- `cargo xtask gate-verdict <dir>...` reads the records below the directories and prints one Markdown verdict. The verdict names each lane, its runner, its time, its result and its record path, then each red step with its note. The exit code is 0 for green and 1 for red.
- Refusals, each with a message:
  - `--lane` on a tier that is not `batch`.
  - A lane that is not `N/M` with `1 <= N <= M <= 16`.
  - A lane with no step.
- The verdict is red when a lane has no record, has two records, is void, ran fewer steps than its plan, or has a record that cannot be read.
- `xtask/src/exec.rs`: the field `clock` of `Run` is `pub(crate)`, so that the record can read the wall time.
- `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`: a section "Batch lanes for separate runners" and the flag row.
- `docs/decisions/2908-batch-lanes.md`: the decisions.

## Cause

The batch tier had no deterministic way to run as parts. `post-merge.yml` thus runs all 973 steps in one job on one runner, and the second runner waits. A lane job also had no result file that a collector could read.

## Tests

Pins, in `xtask/src/lane_split_tests.rs` and `xtask/src/verdict_tests.rs` (14 tests):

- `each_batch_step_runs_in_exactly_one_lane` (the real batch plan, 1 to 6 lanes: no step lost, no step in two lanes)
- `one_lane_of_one_is_the_whole_batch_plan`
- `a_lane_builds_each_crate_that_it_tests_before_the_tests`
- `the_lanes_share_the_queued_and_the_alone_steps_evenly`
- `the_split_is_the_same_on_each_call_and_reads_no_timing_file`
- `a_bad_lane_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_lane_with_no_step_is_an_error_not_a_green_run`
- `a_record_reads_back_as_written`
- `a_damaged_record_is_an_error`
- `all_lanes_green_is_a_green_verdict_that_names_each_lane`
- `a_red_step_is_named_with_its_lane_runner_and_note`
- `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red`
- `the_runner_name_comes_from_the_environment`
- `the_collector_finds_the_records_of_downloaded_artifacts`

Red before the change: `cargo xtask gate batch --lane 1/2 --dry-run` on `upstream/main` `0306743de` gives `xtask: unknown gate option '--lane'`.

Mutation results (each mutation made the named pin red; the restored code is green):

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| The alone steps get no lane | `each_batch_step_runs_in_exactly_one_lane` and 3 others |
| No build step is kept | `a_lane_builds_each_crate_that_it_tests_before_the_tests`, `one_lane_of_one_is_the_whole_batch_plan` |
| `N > M` is accepted | `a_bad_lane_is_refused_by_name`, `a_damaged_record_is_an_error` |
| An empty lane is not an error | `a_lane_with_no_step_is_an_error_not_a_green_run` |
| `--lane` is accepted on each tier | `a_bad_lane_is_refused_by_name` |
| A missing lane is not a fault | `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red`, `the_collector_finds_the_records_of_downloaded_artifacts` |
| A short lane is not a fault | `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red` |
| A void lane is not a fault | `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red` |
| The red steps are not listed | `a_red_step_is_named_with_its_lane_runner_and_note` |

With the `main.rs` of `upstream/main` restored, the new test modules are not part of the build, and no pin runs. That restore is not a red test. The CLI error above is the red reading.

Readings on Linux:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`xtask unit tests`, 251 s).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --lane 1/3 --dry-run`: 9 builds, then 325 of 973 steps. Lane 3: 324 steps.
- One real lane step: `cargo xtask gate batch --lane 1/3 --only "cl suites: lib"` was green and wrote `lane-result.tsv`.
- `cargo xtask gate-verdict gate-logs` on that one record: verdict RED, exit code 1, "lane 2/3 has no record" and "lane 3/3 has no record". This is correct for one lane of three.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No full lane ran. Only one step of lane 1/3 ran for real.
- No GitHub Actions run. No workflow uses the lanes. The record was not written on a self-hosted runner, so `RUNNER_NAME` was not set (the record said `unknown`).
- Windows and macOS.
- The time balance of the lanes. The lanes have equal step counts, not equal measured times.

## Overlaps

- #2606 (`needs-maintainer`) changes the `report` job of `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`. This PR does not change that file. The workflow part of #2908 waits for the decision on #2606.
- #2787 (`needs-rework`, `conflicts`) changes `parse_gate` and `gate` in `xtask/src/main.rs` (a new tier). It touches the same functions, different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2910 and #2915 list many `xtask/` files because their branches carry a process file sync. They do not change the lane code.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: high

Refs #2908

title: fix(geometry): preserve faces and edges on touching solids
body:
Stacked on #2904 (merge #2904 first)

The prerequisite merged as bac4a96c while this work was in progress.
The merge-base diff now contains only the changes for #2845.

## What changed

- Link contact-face fragments only when a four-use edge has one complete matching.
- Keep existing two-use bodies together. Check all shared edges after the links.
- Preserve the closure, winding and outward-volume checks.
- Keep all incident facets until the feature graph checks the contact. Emit one facet pair for each valid solid.
- Store two edge uses inline. Allocate extra storage only for edges with more uses.
- Enable both known-fail pins for #2845. Add geometry pins for whole-face contact and line-only refusal.
- Require a contour over two closed solids in one model to match the single-block reference cut.

## Cause

A contact face can have no plain boundary edge. Plain-edge links then leave that face apart from its solid.
The feature graph kept only three incident facets. It marked every edge with more than two uses as non-manifold.

The old stitching test called two complete outward cubes one self-touching body because they shared one model.
That fixture is the legal whole-face contact case in this issue. The updated test compares the complete cut and verification result.

## Tests

These four pins failed on unchanged production code. They passed after the fix:

- `solids_that_touch_face_to_face_are_two_outward_bodies`
- `no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`
- `solids_sharing_a_whole_face_slice_as_one_outline`
- `a_whole_contact_face_keeps_each_solids_features`

`sample_ap214.step` had 216 tangent edge pairs that picked apart. The pin now finds none.
The face-to-face stack changed from one `NonManifold` verdict to two `Outward` bodies.

The pairing unit tests pass. They cover ambiguity, odd and unbalanced uses, zero edges, invalid apices and pinched bodies.
The full winding, feature, slicing and shared-face safety suites pass. The sample generates finish and pocket paths with no gouge.

Mutation checks:

- Restore the old upstream slicer caller: the slice pin fails. Restore the fix: it passes.
- Restore the old upstream winding caller: the winding pin fails. Restore the fix: it passes.
- Restore the old upstream feature builder: the feature pin fails. Restore the fix: it passes.
- Restore the parent's old slicer: `touching_closed_solids_in_one_model_cut_as_their_union` fails. Restore the fix: it passes.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` selected the batch plan. It completed 972 steps.
971 steps passed. The only failure was the old refusal assertion for the legal whole-face contact fixture.
After that expected-change test was updated, the failed-step gate passed all six `stitch_cross` tests.
Production code did not change between these gate runs.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
The full gate's clippy check also passed for all eight crates.

## Final-head verification requested by review

Head: `75afc26f19d06abd752517a449a46d38c362f5af`.
The head and source files did not change during these checks.

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` reached the motion and app heavy lanes.
The command completed 229 steps in 65.8 minutes and exited with status 1.
228 steps passed or produced the expected result for a known-fail pin. One step had an unexpected failure.

| Heavy lane | Result |

| Motion | 56 tests passed. Two known-fail pins failed as expected. |
| App | 40 tests passed. Five known-fail pins failed as expected. One test failed unexpectedly. |

All six sample bands in `shared_face_bodies_finish` passed with no gouge.

The unexpected failure was `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.
It stopped at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144:5` with the path tuple `(3158, 3130, 1141)`.
The diagnostic reported 3158 moves, 3130 planar moves and 1141 arcs.
Its notes said that some fitted arcs could not be proved inside the cutter-centre area and stayed as chords.
The heavy gate is red. These results do not establish whether this PR caused the failure.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` selected the batch plan and passed all 972 steps in 91.5 minutes.

title: fix(chamfer): a wall that leans in the frame is not a modelled chamfer
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer with no picks generates again on a box stock under a tilted frame.
The check of #2887 no longer reads a wall that leans in the operation frame as a modelled chamfer.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`: the new functions `leans` and `centroid`, the constant `LEAN_SLACK`, and one call in `partly_bevelled`.
- `docs/decisions/2936-chamfer-leaning-wall.md`: the decision record.

No fixture changes. `crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs` is not touched.

## Cause

The fixture of #1700 is a 70 x 70 x 20 box stock with no part. The operation frame is tilted 10 degrees.
In that frame the top section (Z10) and the corner section (Z9) are the same rectangle. The top section is moved 0.176327 mm (`1 mm * tan(10 deg)`) in Y.
`partly_bevelled` (#2887, PR #2894) compares each segment of the top loop with the wall loop.
It read the segments that touch the moved corners as bevelled. It read the middle segments of the X sides as sharp.
It then refused the loop with "carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length".
No edge of the box carries a chamfer. The refusal was wrong for this model.

The loops of the fixture (from a debug print, not committed):

- top: X -35..35, Y -33.776662..37.303201
- corner: X -35..35, Y -33.952989..37.126874

## The fix

`leans(top, wall)` is true when the top loop is the wall loop moved whole by one plan vector.
The vector is the difference of the two area centroids. A collinear vertex does not change an area centroid.
Each segment of each ring (two ends and the middle) must then be on the other ring within `LEAN_SLACK` (1e-4 mm).
When `leans` is true, `partly_bevelled` returns `None`. `ride_loops` then rides the wall at the corner depth, as it did before #2887.

A loop that carries a bevel on part of its length is not a moved copy of its wall. Its bevelled side moves in and its sharp sides stay.
Thus the refusal of #2887 holds for each case that it was written for.

## Tests

Pins:

- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_wall_leaning_in_the_frame_is_not_a_modelled_chamfer` (motion lib, new). It uses the loops of the fixture.
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_moved_outline_with_one_side_bevelled_still_refuses` (motion lib, new). It guards the other direction.
- `framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` (app, `stock_source_holes`, not changed). This is the test of the issue.

Red before the fix, on `upstream/main` afbf1590e:

- The app test fails with the text of the issue (`... carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length - it is sharp near X-35.000 Y-16.176 ...`).
- The new unit pin fails with the same text.

Mutation results:

- The call `leans(top, wall)` disabled: the new unit pin is red, and the app test is red with the text of the issue. Restored: the two are green.
- `leans` replaced by `true`: `a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name`, `a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_with_an_extra_vertex_too` and `a_moved_outline_with_one_side_bevelled_still_refuses` are red. Restored: green.

The old file was not copied back whole, because the new tests are in the same file. The disabled call gives the old behaviour.

Gate on the final source:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 4 steps, 0 failed (motion lib, `chamfer_modelled_edge`, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test stock_source_holes`: 9 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test chamfer_partly_bevelled --test chamfer_modelled_edge`: 2 and 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The quick gate did not select `stock_source_holes`. Its gate map does not name `motion::machining2d::chamfer_ride`. I ran the suite by hand.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes and the release tier.
- A tilted frame on a part with curved walls. The unit pin uses a rectangle only.
- A part with a draft wall on some sides only, in an upright frame. Its two sections are the same as those of a modelled chamfer on those sides. The check of #2887 still refuses it and asks for picks. This PR does not change that.
- macOS and Windows.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs` or the `stock_source_holes` files.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer with no picks on a stock or part whose walls lean in a tilted operation frame generates again; it was refused as "a modelled chamfer on only part of its length".

Effort: high

Fixes #2936

title: build(kernel): remove truck-stepio, ruststep and truck-topology; the STEP bench reads recorded truck verdicts
body:
Follows #2918 (merged). Part 3 of #917. Effort: high (worked by the `max` tier at the coordinator's order).

## What changed

- Root `Cargo.toml`: the pins `truck-stepio`, `truck-topology` and `ruststep` are removed. The `[patch.crates-io]` git pin of ruststep (#887) and its rationale text are removed. The truck comment now names the reference kernel and #2922.
- `crates/kernel/Cargo.toml`: the bench dev-dependencies `truck-stepio`, `truck-meshalgo`, `truck-topology` and `ruststep` are removed. The `truck` feature stays.
- `Cargo.lock` (written by cargo): the packages `ruststep`, `ruststep-derive`, `truck-stepio`, `Inflector` and `derive-new` are removed. Old duplicate versions that only ruststep needed are removed too: `itertools 0.10.5`, `proc-macro-crate 1.3.1`, `toml_edit 0.19.15`, `toml_datetime 0.6.11`, `winnow 0.5.40`.
- Kernel STEP bench: the truck side is now a recorded reading (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement/rows.rs`). The numbers come from the bench's own printout at `4b694c7c7`, before this change. The live solidcore reading is judged against them with the same rules and tolerances. Every pinned verdict string is the same as before.
- `step_agreement.rs` (498 lines) is split along its seam: `rows.rs` (316), `verdict.rs` (168), `step_agreement.rs` (249). This meets #2800.
- `step_util/truck_guard.rs` and `truck_read` in `step_util/mod.rs` are removed.
- `step_import.rs`: the third column of `KNOWN_STEP_VERDICTS` (truck) stays as a record and is not asserted. The truck-only test `truck_side_refuses_a_runaway_face_and_obeys_its_cancel` is replaced by `step_agreement.rs` `recorded_truck_readings_keep_their_findings`.
- `mesh_deviation_bench.rs` (release lane): the truck column is removed. It was printed and never asserted. The recorded numbers of `917-kernel-pcurves.md` are for two files that are not rows of this bench.
- Stale comments: `kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs`, `kernel/tests/heal_import.rs`, `app/tests/import.rs` (#887 test doc), `app/src/geometry/import/step_depth.rs`.
- License notices (`assets/ui/LICENSES.md`, `site/static/icons/LICENSES.txt`): `truck-stepio` is removed. The notices of the truck crates that stay are kept.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2790-remove-truck-step.md`.

## Scope (the maintainer, 2026-11-20)

- This PR removes `truck-stepio`, `ruststep` and `truck-topology` as dependencies of the workspace.
- The non-STEP `TruckKernel` stays: `crates/kernel/src/truck_impl.rs`, the `truck` feature, and the tests `agreement.rs`, `blend.rs`, `heal_import.rs`. Its removal is #2922 (Part of #27).
- Thus the first "Done means" item of #917 ("no `truck-*` package in `Cargo.lock`") is met for the STEP crates only. Nine `truck-*` packages stay in the lock: `truck-base`, `truck-derivers`, `truck-geometry`, `truck-geotrait`, `truck-meshalgo`, `truck-modeling`, `truck-polymesh`, `truck-shapeops`, `truck-topology`.
- `truck-topology` stays in the lock as a transitive package of `truck-meshalgo`, `truck-modeling` and `truck-shapeops`. No member names it.

## Remaining truck uses (all non-STEP)

- `crates/kernel/src/truck_impl.rs`: `TruckKernel` (booleans through `truck-shapeops`, measure through `truck-meshalgo` tessellation, solids through `truck-modeling`).
