title: fix(kernel): divide a runaway strip face over its boundary nodes
body:
## What changed

- The kernel seam divides a face with a runaway triangle count a second time, over its boundary nodes only.
- The new division is the Delaunay fill of the boundary loop of the face. It adds no node. It keeps each shared edge node as it is.
- The seam keeps the new division only when `mesh_deviation::measure_within` proves it inside the tolerance. If not, the face keeps the triangles of the planner.
- The measure of the whole plan runs after that, as before. The guarantee of a machining mesh does not change.
- A kept division is a note in the mesh report: `face N: divided over its K boundary nodes (...)`.
- The known-fail marker of the thread flank test is removed. The test runs in the default suite again.

New files:

- `crates/kernel/src/mesh_redivide.rs`: the selection of the faces, the boundary loop, the checks, the measure.
- `crates/kernel/src/mesh_redivide_fill.rs`: the polygon fill (ear clipping, then Lawson flips).
- `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_redivide.rs`: the test of the tolerance gate.
- `docs/decisions/2844-strip-division.md`: the decisions.

A face is divided again only if it has 10 000 planned triangles or more, and 16 or more for each boundary node. A face with a hole, a pole or a period is not divided.

## Cause

solidcore-tess plans the long, thin helicoid strip isotropically. Our seam (`machining_mesh::planned`) could only pick the chord. The replan at half the chord made the count larger.

Options 1 and 2 of the issue are changes in `NeoTech/solidcore`. This PR is option 3 of the issue comment of 2026-11-20: the seam replaces the inside division of one face.

## Readings

Four-turn thread flank at 5e-3 mm, debug build:

| Plan | Planner | Boundary division | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| chord 5e-3 mm | 274192 triangles | 926 triangles | 7.3e-3 mm, not kept |
| chord 2.5e-3 mm (replan) | 391338 triangles | 1150 triangles | 3.8e-3 mm, kept |

The test time is 35 s. It was 68 s.

## Tests (pins, mutation results)

Pins:

- `a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_at_full_fidelity_in_a_bounded_count` (app, `import_step_thread`). Red on unchanged code: `facet count over the bound: 391338 facets for a four-turn strip`. Green with the fix. All its other asserts stay as they were.
- `a_wide_twisted_face_keeps_the_planner_division` (kernel, `machining_mesh_redivide`).
- `mesh_redivide::tests::a_face_is_divided_over_its_boundary_nodes_with_the_same_boundary_and_sense` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide::tests::a_face_that_is_not_a_plain_region_of_its_shared_nodes_is_not_divided` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide_fill::tests::a_long_strip_is_filled_with_short_sides_across_it` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide_fill::tests::collinear_runs_and_a_notch_keep_every_boundary_side` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide_fill::tests::a_polygon_that_cannot_be_filled_is_refused` (kernel lib).

Mutations:

| Mutation | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `machining_mesh.rs` from `upstream/main` (no call) | the thread flank pin | red (391338 facets), then green after the restore |
| the tolerance gate in `redivide` removed | `a_wide_twisted_face_keeps_the_planner_division` | red (`FaceCapped`), then green |
| the Lawson flips removed | `a_long_strip_is_filled_with_short_sides_across_it` | red (a side 99.75 long), then green |
| the check of the last ear removed | `a_polygon_that_cannot_be_filled_is_refused` | red, then green |

Gate on the final head `48071efd4`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 10 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- These app suites also ran in debug and are green: `contour_whole_step`, `fixture_step_library`, `import_step_closed_shell`, `import_step_corner_blend`, `import_step_curve_guard`, `import_step_doubly_curved`, `import_step_guard`, `import_step_guard_default_cap`, `import_step_open_shell`, `import_step_outward`, `import_step_twisted_flank`, `model_fidelity`, `step_budget`, `step_chord_units`, `step_fidelity`.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes did not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 246 release steps. A reviewer must run them before this PR is ready.
- The 14-turn faces of the user's parts (#1602) did not run. Their boundary has about 4000 nodes, under the bound of 8192 vertices of the fill.
- No face with a hole was divided: the code refuses such a face before the fill.
- The time of the planner itself does not change. The planner still makes its isotropic division, and the replan at half the chord remains. The speed item of #2780 stays open.
- solidcore-tess stays at the pinned rev. No dependency changed.

## Overlaps

- #2918 touches `crates/kernel/src/lib.rs` (the same file, different lines). Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2795 touches `crates/app/tests/import_step_thread.rs` (the same file, a different function: `flank_step`). Whichever merges second refreshes.

Effort: max

Changelog: A STEP thread flank (a long, thin helical strip) meshes in about 1000 facets, not 391 000; the kernel divides such a face over its edge nodes and keeps the division only when it measures inside the tolerance (#2844).

Fixes #2844

title: fix(mcp): accept an explicit zero taper on a wire contour
body:
Accept an explicit zero taper when a script or MCP client adds or edits a Wire Contour. The patch validator reads the typed operation value when the saved form omits its default. Other operation kinds and unknown fields retain their existing checks.

The regression test wire_contour_accepts_an_explicit_zero_taper_on_add_and_edit creates a vertical operation, sets a taper and clears it. It also checks a misspelled field and a field on the wrong operation kind.

The quick gate passed all 16 steps and 373 tests. Strict clippy passed on all camcraft-app targets. The normal CLI produced the same 331-byte vertical program for an omitted taper, zero, 0.0 and an edit from 3 degrees to zero. The 3 degree control produced 496 bytes. A misspelled field, a wire taper on a Face operation, and a string value each failed without an NC file. The release suite pocket3d_hsm failed on macOS (Apple silicon). The measured triple was 3158 moves, 3130 planar moves and 1141 arcs. Base commit 3ffe2338f reproduced these three counts and failed the same assertion. See #2371. The remaining heavy suites are running. Verification used the offline software only.

Effort: high
Changelog: A Wire Contour accepts an explicit zero taper on creation and when an edit returns it to a vertical cut.

Fixes #2925

title: feat(ui): Display menu quality preset, ground shadow, ambient occlusion and Look at a work plane
body:
Stacked on #2835 (merge #2835 first).

## What changed

- The Graphics group of the Display menu has four new rows:
  - "Performance" and "Quality": the quality presets (one choice).
  - "Ground shadow": a soft shadow of the model on the floor.
  - "Ambient occlusion": darker shading in the corners of the model.
- The Look at group has a new entry: "Look at a work plane".
- Each entry has a tooltip. Each entry is view state. No entry queues a command.
- A preset sets the two switches. "Performance" sets the two off. "Quality" sets the two on.
- The menu shows the active preset. The active preset is derived from the switches. If the user changes one switch, no preset is active.
- The two switches are saved in the per-user `view.json`. An old file without the keys loads them off. The default is off, so the view of #2818 does not change.
- Ground shadow: the model bodies are projected straight down on the floor (`floor::floor_z`). The footprint is sampled on a grid, blurred, and drawn as blended triangles (`ground_shadow`). The draw list has the new step `Pipe::GroundShadow`, after the model and before the stock.
- Ambient occlusion: each model vertex gets one baked value (`occlusion`). The value is the share of short rays over the face that meet the body again. The draw list has the new step `Pipe::FacesOccluded`. It is the face shader with the baked value on its light. The values are a second vertex buffer. The model vertex buffer does not change.
- The shadow data and the occlusion data are cached (`shade_cache`):
  - The shadow key is the facets and the shown pose of each body, and the floor height.
  - The occlusion key is the facets of one body. A moved body keeps its values.
  - A switch that is off builds nothing. A still frame builds nothing.
- Wireframe draws no lit face and no shadow. The two switches are disabled in Wireframe. They keep their values, and their tooltip says why.
- No entry is hidden on wasm. The two passes are vertex buffers and alpha blending in the one wgpu pass that the two shells share. They use no texture.
- "Look at a work plane" arms one click on an origin axis in the view. The view turns to face the plane of that axis: Z gives XY, X gives YZ, Y gives ZX. A click on the origin point gives the XY plane. The origins are the work offsets (WCS) and the world origin. The view does not pan or zoom. A miss changes nothing and says so.
- `world_verts` moved from `egui_app/world.rs` to the new `egui_app/world_verts.rs`. The code is the same. `world.rs` was at 392 lines and the new scene data put it past 400.

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for in #2818. #2834 is the part that #2835 does not include.

## Screenshots

`examples/guide-workholding.camproj`. The stock and the toolpaths are hidden, so that the model shows.

| Before ("Performance") | After ("Quality") |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/before-performance.png) | ![after quality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-quality.png) |

| "Ground shadow" only | "Ambient occlusion" only |
|---|---|
| ![shadow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-ground-shadow.png) | ![occlusion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-ambient-occlusion.png) |

| The Display menu | After "Look at a work plane", a click on the X axis of G54 |
|---|---|
| ![menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-display-menu.png) | ![look at](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-look-at-yz-plane.png) |

The screenshots come from the off-screen harness of the guide images, on a software GPU. They are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. No image is in this branch.

## Tests

Pins (all new, all green on the head):

- `ui::draw_list::tests` (3 new tests): the draw list with the shadow pass and with the occlusion pass, on and off.
  - `the_ground_shadow_pass_draws_after_the_model_and_before_the_stock`
  - `the_occlusion_pass_takes_the_model_face_slot`
  - `the_longest_draw_list_holds_each_pass`
- `egui_app::tests::display_quality` (8 tests): the menu.
  - `each_quality_switch_sets_its_field_and_shows_the_check`
  - `a_preset_sets_its_switches_and_one_changed_switch_leaves_no_preset`
  - `wireframe_disables_the_two_switches_and_keeps_their_values`
  - `the_quality_switches_are_kept_in_the_view_file`
  - `look_at_turns_the_view_to_face_a_picked_work_plane`
  - `a_click_on_the_origin_point_gives_the_xy_work_plane`
  - `look_at_a_plane_away_from_each_axis_changes_nothing_and_says_so`
  - `arming_one_look_at_pick_disarms_the_other`
- `shade_cache::tests` (4 tests): the counter tests and the changed-input tests.
  - `a_still_frame_builds_no_shadow_data_and_a_moved_body_builds_again`
  - `a_still_frame_builds_no_occlusion_data_and_new_facets_build_again`
  - `switches_that_are_off_build_no_shade_data`
  - `the_scene_digest_follows_the_shade_data`
- `occlusion::tests` (3 tests), `ground_shadow::tests` (3 tests): the data, with degenerate input.
- `look_at_plane::tests` (2 tests), `display_quality::tests` (1 test).
- `gpu_render::the_ground_shadow_darkens_the_ground_and_not_the_model` and `gpu_render::the_occlusion_pass_darkens_model_faces_only`: a real GPU pass. They compile the new shader stages.
- `view_file::the_shading_switches_round_trip_and_an_old_file_loads_them_off` (`camcraft-app`).

Red before the change: yes. The pins name new items, so they did not compile on the unchanged head of #2835 (`ui lib: FAIL, compile error`). The mutation checks below show that each guard is pinned.

- `draw_list_tests.rs` and `view_file.rs` build `Counts` and `ViewPrefs` with `..Default::default()`. Each structure has two new fields.

The picked face normal now uses `setup_align::view_pose`, as drawing and picking do. This includes the active setup alignment.

`egui_app::tests::display_menu::look_at_uses_the_face_normal_in_the_active_setup_frame` pins a setup rotated 90 degrees about X. It asserts the shown -Y normal and the camera direction after the click.

- The UI library had 1308 passed, 7 failed, and 7 ignored tests. Six report tests failed with `No adapter found`. `headless_run_succeeds` reported `metal found no adapters`.

- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN in 1 minute 1 second.

## Goldens moved

## Not exercised

title: feat(ui): "Wireframe, see-through" display mode
body:
Stacked on #2835 (merge #2835 first).

## What changed

- The Display menu has a fifth display mode: "Wireframe, see-through". It stands after "Wireframe".
- The mode draws each edge of the model and of the stock, front and back.
- The mode draws no face. No face goes to the color buffer. No face goes to the depth buffer.
- The model hides nothing behind it: not the stock, not a fixture, not a toolpath.
- A click in the mode picks hidden edges too. The "Pick through" switch stays as the user set it.
- The wireframe switch of the toolbar shows as active in the two wireframe modes. One press in either mode gives "Shaded, with edges".
- The view file stores the mode with the key `wireframe-see-through`.
- The traced stock is a shaded surface. The mode draws the stock wire in its place, as "Wireframe" does.

#2835 gives the other parts of #2636: "Shaded" (faces, no edges), the draw list of each mode, and the saved display mode. This PR adds only the mode that #2835 left out.

The picking rule of the mode:

1. Each edge can be picked, front or back.
2. The edge that draws nearest to the cursor wins.
3. When two edges draw at the same distance from the cursor, the edge nearest to the camera wins.

This is the existing rule of `camcraft_app::pick::pick_bodies` with `through`. The mode asks for `through`.

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for in #2636. The viewport had no wireframe mode that shows the hidden edges.

title: fix(wire): refuse work outside the stated guide heights
body:
Check the work height against each stated wire guide before the post writes NC. Compare both heights in world coordinates. Use the operation, the part and the stock to determine the full work height.

A 3 degree taper through 12 mm of stock previously posted 496 bytes with its upper guide at Z5. The normal CLI now refuses this case and creates no output file. A 0.001 mm overrun also fails. A fractional setup origin that puts the work exactly at the guide passes.

The valid vertical and tapered control programs match their original NC files byte for byte. A straight cut still accepts a machine with no stated guide heights.

The pinning tests are work_above_the_upper_guide_blocks_the_post and the shifted-stock test in wire_taper. The quick gate passed all six steps, including all 291 app library tests. The release suite pocket3d_hsm failed on macOS (Apple silicon). The measured triple was 3158 moves, 3130 planar moves and 1141 arcs. Base commit 3ffe2338f reproduced these three counts and failed the same assertion. See #2371. The remaining heavy suites are running. The verification also used the normal command script, all 10 related wire suites (62 tests), and strict clippy on all camcraft-app targets.

The offline 40 by 20 mm punch comparison used the same nominal geometry in three tools. The two Agie generators agreed on the nominal contour. CamCraft put its wire center 0.165 mm outside each face. The offline Agie control formally checked and plotted its native vertical bundle. Its technology added its own trim offsets. It did not run the CamCraft generic program or verify a tapered cut.

Effort: high
Changelog: Wire EDM refuses a post when the work extends past a stated guide height.

Fixes #2923

title: fix(import): preserve STEP short-name length units
body:
## What changed

The model importer expands `GUAC` and `SUNT` in the parsed STEP records.
The unit checks and topology reader then use the same long names.
Short-name inch and metre models keep their correct size in millimetres.

## Cause

The pinned parser expands some short names but leaves these two unchanged.
The unit reader only finds the long names.
It can miss the unit context and silently assume millimetres.

The mappings come from the public [ISO short-name registry](https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt).
The fixtures use our unit-box geometry.

## Tests

- `short_name_inch_import_keeps_scale`
- `short_name_metre_import_keeps_scale`
- `short_context_only_import_keeps_scale`
- `short_si_unit_only_import_keeps_scale`
- `long_name_context_controls_import_with_correct_scale`

The four regression tests failed before the fix. The long-name controls passed.
All five tests pass with the fix.
The tests check the units, solid count, bounding coordinates, and volume.

Mutation results:

- Restoring the full upstream source makes all four regressions fail. Restoring the fix passes all five tests.
- Removing the `GUAC` mapping fails its isolated test. Restoring it passes.
- Removing the `SUNT` mapping fails its isolated test. Restoring it passes.

The two new fixture rows are in `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement/rows.rs` after the merge of main.
`step_short_units_inch` and `step_short_units_metre` remain.
The rows keep the recorded legacy reader refusals.
The removed reader stays removed.
`recorded_truck_readings_keep_their_findings` checks both refusal readings.
Removing each row makes its per-file test fail. Restoring each row passes.
Changing each refusal makes the preservation pin fail. Restoring each refusal passes.

Final validation on head `20214c9f8cd0f1614e415281a3b69ce389c25d7c`:

- STEP agreement suite: 25 tests passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: all 82 steps passed; 2046 tests passed; 33 ignored; 13.1 minutes.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: all 249 steps passed; 44.2 minutes.
- Kernel heavy lane: passed; 4 tests passed.
- Motion heavy lane: passed; 56 tests passed.
- App heavy lane: passed; 41 tests passed.
- Known-fail checks: all nine checks failed at their expected assertions and passed the gate checks.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed; exit 0; 51.6 seconds.

The final gates ran on this unchanged head.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` files changed.

## Not exercised

No physical machine, release gate, or manual GUI import was exercised.
This change does not repair the raw tessellator or the legacy STEP reader.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes the touched files.
PR #2918 changes the tool-body reader in other files.

title: feat(2d): Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains
body:
Stacked on #2716 (merge #2716 first)

This branch starts at the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`). The diff against `main` shows the changes of #2716 too, until #2716 merges. The changes of this PR are the one commit `feat(2d): Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains`.

## What changed

- A `Slot` and a `Trochoidal Slot` now take one picked chain of a DXF profile (`FeatureSel::SketchChain` or a `SketchLayer` that holds one chain).
- One closed line-arc slot outline seeds `a`, `b` and `width`.
- One open straight chain is the centerline. It seeds `a` and `b`. The typed `width` stays.
- The pick seeds in its own command (`CreateOperation`, `SetOperationGeometry`). One undo takes back the pick and the seed. This is the law of #1504.
- Generation judges the stored slot against the picked chain. A slot that left its outline is refused by name. A slot whose ends are not the ends of its centerline is refused by name.
- The verification and the stock simulation use the setup stock (`part_solid = false`), as #2716 does for the 2D Contour.
- The project file does not change. A `.camproj` file with a two-point slot opens and generates as before.

These picks are refused by name:

- a closed chain that is not a slot outline (a rectangle, a circle): "is not a slot outline";
- an open chain that is not straight: "the picked centerline is not straight";
- more than one chain: "a slot on a DXF profile cuts one chain, and this selection has 2 chains";
- the whole profile as the source: "needs one picked chain";
- a channel narrower than the tool. The `Slot` refusal now gives the slot width and the tool diameter.

Files:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_line.rs` (new): `SlotBound::from_centerline`, `SlotBound::centerline` and the ends law.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room.rs`: the `Room::Line` kind in each match of the room law.

Readings from the outline pin (4 mm tool, 10 mm outline, centres (45, 25) and (75, 25)):

- seeded ends (45.000, 25.000) and (75.000, 25.000), width 10.000 mm;
- cutter centre X 42.000 to 78.000 and Y 22.000 to 28.000;

|---|---|
| M1 outline area test off | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) |

title: fix(import): read the tool coordinate systems, units and diagnostics through the solidcore p21 parser
body:
Follows #2904 (merged). Part 2 of #917.

## What changed

- The tool coordinate-system reader, the length-unit reader and the STEP syntax locator move from `crates/app/src/geometry/import/` to `camcraft-geometry`:
  - `camcraft_geometry::step_csys` (types and `read_tool_csys(text)`) and `step_csys_read` (the reader).
  - `camcraft_geometry::step_units` (`length_unit_mm`).
  - `camcraft_geometry::step_diag` (`locate`; each DATA record is now checked with the solidcore Part 21 parser).
- The readers use `camcraft_kernel::p21`. This is a one-line re-export of `solidcore_step::p21`. The solidcore pin stays in the kernel manifest only. There is no new edge between our crates.
- The app keeps `step_csys.rs` as a thin wrapper: the nesting scan, the empty and UTF-8 checks, and the map to `ImportError`. It re-exports the types, so the callers (`tool_body*`, MCP) do not change.
- `step_depth` code does not change. It stays the nesting law in front of every read. Its documents now say why.
- `ruststep` is removed from `crates/app/Cargo.toml`. `Cargo.lock` loses only the app edge. The root pin and the kernel dev-dependencies stay for part 3 (#2790).
- In the browser build (wasm32), `read_tool_csys` refuses by name, as the model import already does.
- Review fix: the unit reader refuses a file that has a length unit when no unit context states a length unit (see "Readings").

## Readings (decisions in `docs/decisions/2789-step-readers-solidcore.md`)

- An entity id that is defined two times: the reader refuses the file by name. ruststep kept the last definition and the new parser keeps the first. No tracked fixture has a duplicate id.
- A file with no DATA section: the reader refuses it with the old text "file has no DATA section".
- Several DATA sections: the reader reads them as one (ISO 10303-21 edition 3). The old reader read only the first.
- A syntax error of the tool-body read has the wording of the model import now (the entity, its line and its text).
- The nesting limit: the parser has its own cap of 64. But it accepts an empty innermost `()` one level past that cap. The scan refuses that record. Both sides are pinned.
- A length unit that no unit context states: the read is refused by name. The parser maps short names such as `A2PL3D` and `LNGUNT`, but not the short forms of `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `SI_UNIT`. Thus a short-name tool file gave a CIP but no unit context, and the reader used 1 mm per unit. The refusal applies when the file has one of these records:
  - a `LENGTH_UNIT`;
  - an `SI_UNIT` of the metre;
  - a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT` over a `LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT`.
  The refusal text is "length unit #N is in the file, but no GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT states a length unit ...". A file with no unit record keeps 1 mm per unit, as the ruststep reader did. The reader does not guess the two short names: no public source in the repository or in the solidcore checkout states them.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/step_csys_read.rs` (new, 11): `the_fixture_reads_through_the_part_21_parser`, `an_entity_id_defined_twice_is_refused_by_name`, `a_file_with_no_data_section_is_refused_by_its_old_text`, `several_data_sections_are_read_as_one`, `a_syntax_error_names_the_entity_and_its_line`, `the_parser_alone_takes_an_empty_list_one_past_its_depth_cap`, `corrupt_input_is_a_clean_error_never_a_panic`, and for the units:
  - `a_short_name_tool_file_in_inches_or_metres_is_refused_by_name`;
  - `a_short_name_tool_file_with_a_long_unit_context_reads_at_its_scale` (inch 25.4, metre 1000, millimetre 1);
  - `a_long_name_tool_file_in_inches_reads_at_twenty_five_point_four`;
  - `a_tool_file_with_no_unit_record_keeps_millimetres`.
- `crates/geometry/tests/step_units.rs` (new, 6): the 4 in-file tests of the app, moved, `a_unit_that_converts_to_itself_is_refused_at_the_chain_cap`, and `a_length_unit_that_no_context_states_is_refused_by_name` (an angle-only file still keeps millimetres).
- `crates/geometry/tests/step_diag.rs` (new, 4): the locator wording ("cannot be parsed", "no DATA section found", "is never closed") and the records that pass.
- `crates/app/tests/step_nesting.rs`: new `an_empty_list_one_past_the_cap_is_refused_by_the_scan`.
- Not changed and green: `tool_csys` (11), `step_nesting` (9), `import` (26), `import_step_closed_shell` (6), `tool_body` (12), `tool_body_assembly` (5), `tool_body_view` (7), `mcp_tool_body` (5), geometry `step_metre_unit` (1).
- The `#[test]` count goes up by 18: 22 tests are added (4 of them moved from the app) and 4 app unit tests are removed.

## Gate

First head (a29d79a65 merged with main), run before the review:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test step_units --test step_csys_read --test step_diag --test step_metre_unit`: 17 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_csys --test step_nesting --test import --test tool_body --test tool_body_assembly --test tool_body_view --test mcp_tool_body --test import_step_closed_shell`: 81 passed.
- `cargo check -p camcraft-geometry --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: builds (one old warning in `step.rs`, not from this PR).

Review fix (head 4b694c7c7, after `git merge origin/main`):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test step_units --test step_csys_read --test step_diag`: 21 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_csys --test step_nesting --test tool_body --test mcp_tool_body`: 37 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The batch tier and the heavy lanes. The model-import suites outside the lists above were not run. `import`, `tool_body_assembly`, `tool_body_view`, `import_step_closed_shell` and `step_metre_unit` were not run again on the review-fix head.
- The full browser build (`web/build-app-wasm.sh`). Only the geometry crate was checked for wasm32, and only on the first head.
- Real vendor tool files with string escapes (`\X2\...`). The new parser decodes them; ruststep did not. No fixture has them.
- Real short-name tool files: the pins use hand-made text.

## Follow-up

- #2919: the model import has the same unit gap in the kernel's `length_units`. That is a separate PR.

Changelog: The tool-body STEP reader refuses a file in which an entity id is defined two times, refuses a file whose length unit no unit context states, and reads all DATA sections of a file.

Refs #917

Fixes #2789

title: feat(sim): generate a loose machine model posed by axis values
body:
## What changed

- The PR adds the module `camcraft_sim::machine_model`.
- The input is plain data of the module: `MachineSpec` and `PartSpec` (parts, parent, joint kind, axis, pivot, offset, travel, spindle body, tool station).
- `camcraft-sim` gets no edge to `camcraft-post`. The caller (#2586) maps `MachineTree` into the input.
- `generate` makes one closed body for each part that states a number:
  - a block for a table, a bed or a slide, sized from `travel`;
  - a cylinder for the spindle body, sized from the spindle diameter and length;
  - a cylinder for the tool envelope, sized from the tool station. Its kind is `BodyKind::ToolEnvelope`. It is not steel.
- `MachineModel::pose` moves the bodies along the joint chain for a set of axis values. It handles linear joints, rotary joints, a pivot and an offset.
- Each body has `BodySource::Generated`. `BodySource::judged_on()` gives "judged on a generated model".
- A part with no number gets no body and a named note in `MachineModel::notes`. No size is guessed.
- Degenerate input refuses with the part id and the key. No path panics.
- `docs/decisions/2584-machine-model.md` records the decisions.

## Cause

This is new work, not a defect. `camcraft-sim` had no machine model. The maintainer asked for a loose model from the machine file (#2574).

## Tests

Pins, in `crates/sim/tests/machine_model.rs`:

- `vmc_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`
- `tilt_head_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`
- `a_rotary_turns_about_its_pivot_and_a_part_sits_at_its_offset`
- `each_body_is_closed_and_marked_generated`
- `a_part_with_no_number_gets_no_body_and_a_named_note`

Pins, in `crates/sim/tests/machine_model_refusals.rs`:

- `the_plain_input_generates_and_poses`
- `travel_must_be_finite_with_max_over_min`
- `a_joint_axis_must_be_a_finite_direction`
- `positions_must_be_finite`
- `spindle_and_tool_station_sizes_must_be_real_lengths`
- `the_part_list_must_be_a_tree_with_unique_ids`
- `a_pose_states_each_joint_one_time_with_a_finite_value`

Red before the change: yes. On unchanged code the suite did not compile, because the module did not exist.

Mutation results: 32 mutations, one at a time. Each one made a pin red. The restored tree is green.

| Guard removed or changed | Red pin |
|---|---|
| length finite, length more than zero, length maximum | `spindle_and_tool_station_sizes_must_be_real_lengths` |
| position finite, position maximum | `positions_must_be_finite` |
| axis finite, axis not zero | `a_joint_axis_must_be_a_finite_direction` |
| travel on a fixed part, travel finite, travel zero or reversed, travel maximum | `travel_must_be_finite_with_max_over_min` |
| no part, too many parts, blank id, repeated id, parent order | `the_part_list_must_be_a_tree_with_unique_ids` |
| pose value finite, pose value maximum, two values, unknown part, fixed part, missing value | `a_pose_states_each_joint_one_time_with_a_finite_value` |
| chain order of the frames | `tilt_head_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`, `a_rotary_turns_about_its_pivot_and_a_part_sits_at_its_offset` |
| pivot, offset | `a_rotary_turns_about_its_pivot_and_a_part_sits_at_its_offset` |
| circumscribed round face | `each_body_is_closed_and_marked_generated` |
| stack over the spindle, stack under the table | `vmc_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`, `tilt_head_bodies_at_two_axis_positions` |
| table needs X and Y travel, no travel gives no block | `a_part_with_no_number_gets_no_body_and_a_named_note` |
| the words "judged on a generated model" | `each_body_is_closed_and_marked_generated` |

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on the final tree: sim lib, `machine_model`, `machine_model_refusals`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` is green. The first run found one `needless_range_loop` in `shape.rs`. That is fixed.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` file and no `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- `pose` has a last check that each posed vertex is finite. The input checks ahead of it stop each non-finite value. Thus no test reaches it. It stays as a backstop.
- The winding flip of a block face for a left-handed basis. The pinned axes give right-handed bases.
- A slide on a skew axis (not along X, Y or Z). The code handles it, but no pin has one.
- The mapping from `MachineTree` to `MachineSpec`. It is the work of #2586. The tilt-head pin maps `assets/machines/tilthead.mch` by hand.
- No check uses the bodies yet. The collision of machine parts is #2586.
- The batch tier and the release tier did not run.

## Notes for the review

- The type is `feat`, because the issue is an enhancement with new behaviour.
- The PR adds no user-facing command. Thus it adds no MCP tool.
- The PR adds no dependency.
- The sizes are loose by design. The ratios are `SECTION_RATIO` (0.25) and `BED_RATIO` (0.1).
- A joint `axis` is the direction in which the part itself moves. The caller reverses it for a part that moves the table. The decision file gives the reason.

## Overlaps

- #2763 touches `crates/sim/src/lib.rs` for a different module line. It touches the same file, different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Effort: high

Changelog: sim: `camcraft_sim::machine_model` generates a loose machine model (blocks and cylinders) from plain part data and poses it by axis values; each body is marked "generated" (#2584).

Fixes #2584

title: docs(examples): add the catalog case 2d/slots
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the example case `examples/catalog/2d/slots`.

- The part is a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block with two closed slots along X. Each slot is 10 mm wide, 6 mm deep and 60 mm long.
- `Slot1` (Slot) cuts the slot at `Y15` in rows, at the levels `Z9` and `Z6`.
- `Trochoidal slot1` (Trochoidal slot) cuts the slot at `Y-15` in 113 loops, at the full depth.
- The two operations use the same tool (`EM-0600-4FL`), the same width and the same floor.
- The README compares the two programs in a table and says what to look at.
- `model/gen_slots_obj.py` writes the mesh. The geometry is original. The script checks that the mesh is watertight and that its top area is correct.
- `docs/decisions/2861-slots-example.md` records the decisions.

No product code changes. The only Rust change is one new test with its helper in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.

## Cause

The case did not exist. The maintainer asked for a set of example cases (#2392).

## The two programs

| | Slot | Trochoidal slot |
|---|---|---|
| Motion blocks | 19 | 803 |
| Arc blocks | 0 | 459 |
| Cut levels | `Z9`, `Z6` | `Z6` only |
| Cutting feed | `F600` | `F1200` |
| Time of the feed moves | 0.60 min | 1.28 min |

## Bug found

#2906: a Slot wider than the tool leaves up to 0.86 mm in its round ends, and `verify` is ok. The rows touch a round end only at their end points. The README names the bug. The bug has a link on #2392.

The work found no refusal and no missing MCP parameter.

## Tests

Pin: `slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor` in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.

- Red before the case: `case 2d/slots must hold .../examples/catalog/2d/slots/slots.nc: No such file or directory`.
- Green with the case.

The two existing catalog tests read each case folder, so they cover the new case without a change:

- `every_catalog_case_opens_regenerates_verifies_and_posts_byte_for_byte`

title: fix(turning): stop reading thread valleys and neck steps as false hidden rest
body:
## What changed

- `crates/sim/src/solid_rest.rs`: store an orientation-free CCW XY angular sector on each boundary `Claim` (keeping `Claim` at 40 bytes). Settle multiple non-coplanar bare-boundary plane groups at one Z level by angular multiplicity: emit 1 crossing when any open angular sector has odd group multiplicity (a manifold meridian seam, cone apex or rim), and 0 when every sector has even multiplicity (a grazing V-root or overhang fold). Keep single coplanar groups at 1 crossing.
- `crates/sim/src/solid_rest_tests.rs`: move the `solid_rest` unit tests to a sibling file (400-line law) and add parity pins for a revolved meridian seam, cone apex, grazing V-root and `Claim` size.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_turned.rs` and `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_hidden.rs`: check strict entry into the open recess `(p, roof)` in `TurnedBand::excuses` instead of inflating the recess and band by `+/-reach`. A pass ending at a neck step (`Z20..Z60`) or starting at the neck top (`Z63..Z78`) no longer claims the neck floor; any pass that enters or bridges `(p, roof)` still owns that floor and convicts.
- `crates/sim/tests/turned_hidden_rest.rs` and `crates/app/tests/turning_hidden_floor.rs`: pin Profile Finish and zero-leave Profile Rough over a cone, a neck (`Z60..Z63`) and M10x1.5 V grooves, plus negative pins that a pass stopping inside the neck still blocks the post.
- `docs/decisions/2880-profile-finish-neck-thread.md`: record the design decision and rejected alternatives.
- `crates/motion/tests/finish3d.rs`: correct the convex-cap heavy test. Preserve the gouge and refused-plunge checks. Pin one material interval at four meridians, judged hidden rest within tolerance, and no false envelope warning.

## Cause

Two separate defects in `camcraft-sim` caused the two false rest readings in #2880:

1. On a 64-segment revolved thread, lattice columns on the 45-degree meridian (`x == y`) lie on the shared edge of two non-coplanar flank facets. `solid_rest::crossings_from_claims` emitted one crossing per non-coplanar boundary group (two crossings per flank), which inverted solid/air parity inside every V-groove and exposed the downward-facing upper flank as a hidden top (`0.7028 mm rest`).
2. `TurnedBand::excuses` inflated the open recess `[p, roof]` and band by `+/-reach` (`+/-(r + floor)`). A cone pass ending at `Z60` (or a thread pass starting at `Z63`) therefore claimed the `Z60..Z63` neck floor (`0.2435 mm rest`), even though no non-gouging tangent ball centre can sit outside the open recess `(60, 63)`.

## Tests

Pins:
- `solid_rest::tests::revolved_meridian_edge_and_v_root_keep_true_parity`
- `solid_rest::tests::claim_stays_forty_bytes`
- `stock_sim::scan_turned::tests::a_pass_stopping_at_a_neck_step_does_not_own_the_neck_recess`
- `turned_hidden_rest::thread_valleys_and_neck_step_at_window_edge_are_not_false_rest`
- `turning_hidden_floor::profile_finish_over_cone_neck_and_thread_posts`
- `finish3d::overhang_entries_are_refused_without_false_hidden_rest`
- `stock_sim::hidden_rest_surfaces_under_a_ceiling` (true hidden-rest control)

Red before fix:
- `full_z20_z78`: `finish envelope near move 20: 0.0117 mm gouge, 0.7028 mm rest`
- `cone_z20_z60`: `finish envelope near move 7: 0.0062 mm gouge, 0.2477 mm rest`
- `rough0_z20_z78`: `finish envelope near move 19855: 0.0117 mm gouge, 0.7028 mm rest`

Mutations on `turned_hidden_rest::thread_valleys_and_neck_step_at_window_edge_are_not_false_rest`:
- Revert `crates/sim/src/solid_rest.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (`thread major ride Z63..Z78: rest 0.8218 > gate 0.05625`); restore: green.
- Revert `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_turned.rs` and `scan_hidden.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (`thread major ride Z63..Z78: rest 2.3735 > gate 0.05625`); restore: green.

Additional mutation for the heavy-lane correction:
- Restore `crates/sim/src/solid_rest.rs` from `upstream/main`: RED. The convex-cap pin finds two zero-width intervals at `(5, 5)` instead of one material interval.
- Restore the PR file: GREEN. The corrected heavy pin and the true hidden-rest control both pass.

Gates on final head `d19a630355c0d30d1780a66c6283a3ced77f9c02`, base `upstream/main` at `58cb641caa0a4c0b6d514c3e874ccaee1b8a6e5b`:
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. Motion and app lanes ran. All 220 steps passed in 29.7 minutes. Motion: 56 test passes. App: 42 test passes. The gate separately checked three known-fail tests for #1950. Each failed as expected. There were no unexpected failures.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 7 steps passed. Sim lib: 195 passed. `hidden_rest_banded`: 5 passed, 1 ignored. `scan_arc`: 2 passed. `turned_hidden_rest`: 6 passed. `turning_hidden_floor`: 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN. No warnings.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The full workspace batch and full release gates did not run. The reached motion and app heavy lanes ran and passed.
- The GUI did not open a turning project.
- The example catalog case `turning/cone-thread` (#2394 / PR #2883) is not on `main` yet and was not rebuilt here.

title: feat(import): read STEP through solidcore (part 1 of #917)
body:
Was stacked on #2843 (`issue/917-kernel-parity`). #2843 is merged as 7173bb44a, and the base of this PR is `main` now.

## What changed

- The app reads a STEP model through solidcore: `camcraft_geometry::step::parse` calls the kernel seam (`import_step_model`, then `machining_mesh` for each solid). `camcraft-app` gets no new edge to `camcraft-kernel`.
- The truck mesh path of the app is removed: 11 `step_*` modules of `crates/app/src/geometry/import/` and the truck dependencies of `crates/app/Cargo.toml`.
- A model over the facet budget is meshed again at a coarser chord. The kept chord goes to `coarse_mm` (#864).
- Each closed solid lands as one facet range (`solids` in the project file, optional, no version step). The slicer and the winding check read the solids from the ranges.
- The shared-edge rule (`shared_edge::solids_touch`) accepts an edge where two closed solids touch along a wall.
- The 2D corner check reads a self-crossing leftover loop by the even-odd rule (`outer_fills`, bc5daa32d).
- `pick/winding.rs` is split: the welder and the union-find move to `pick/winding/weld.rs` (no behaviour change).
- The browser build refuses a STEP file by name.
- Review fixes (head 853522f2e): the face winding check of the kernel reads at most 4 `ORIENTED_FACE` wrappers, its union-find has union by size and path compression, and it reads the cancel token of the import.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/917-solidcore-step.md`.

## Readings

| Fixture | Reading on this branch | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| `fig8.step` | 12590 facets (main 7974), deviation measured within the tolerance | `shoulder_adaptive.rs` (known-fail #2849), decision table "#2844" |
| `fillet_corner.step` | 1866 facets; closed-form volume at the kernel; the bent-weight variant is refused at read ("first #1289 at read: face #1228: weight: ... out of range") | kernel `step_closed_form.rs`, app `import_step_closed_shell.rs` (3 tests) |
| `bar_cross_holes.step` | reads through the kernel pcurves; the tilted cross hole is judged | kernel `step_closed_form.rs`, app `tilted_gouge.rs` |
| `twisted_flank.step` | reads at 7999.857 mm3 (want 8000, tolerance 0.8 mm3), 5132 facets, full fidelity | kernel, geometry and app `step_twisted_flank` tests, app `import_step_twisted_flank.rs` |
| `twisted_flank_off.step` | refused: "#117 at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 3 faces; first: face #93: off the surface's range" | the same three test files |

## Changed, ignored and deleted pins

The decision file has the old reading, the new reading, the cause and the safety argument for each.

- Changed: `import_step_closed_shell.rs`, `import_step_open_shell.rs` test 1, `import_step_guard.rs`, `import_step_guard_default_cap.rs`, `import_step_curve_guard.rs`, `import_step_corner_blend.rs`, `model_fidelity.rs`, `import_step_thread.rs`, `import_step_doubly_curved.rs`, kernel `machining_mesh_parity.rs`, `bore_facet_sagitta.rs`, `step_chord_units.rs`, ui `model_incomplete.rs`. See "Changed pins".
- Restored on the final head (the old assert still holds): the excess floor of `model_fidelity.rs`; the face count and gap text of `import_step_guard_default_cap.rs`; the full "used twice" refusal of `import_step_guard.rs`.
- Made hard on the final head: geometry `step_twisted_flank.rs` (no longer accepts Ok or Err); the bore 0.05 mm pins now assert the blocking warning (`gouge`, "move N cuts past the finish surface").
- Deleted: the 100 `#[test]` of the removed truck modules. See "Removed truck modules (100 `#[test]`)". Four mesh laws with no pin on the new path are filed as #2903 (item 1, `Unmeasured::NoSurface`, is pinned now at the measure step).
- Ignored with the known-fail marker:
  - #2849: `lead_approach.rs` (2 tests), `shoulder_adaptive.rs` (1 test).
  - #2844: `import_step_thread.rs` (1 test).
  - #2845: `feature_edge_g1_join.rs` (1 test), `winding_align.rs` (1 test).
- #2850 makes the same corner-check change. See "#2850 and the corner check" for the merge rule.

## `#[test]` count

Against `issue/917-kernel-parity`: 8660 -> 8587 (-73). The 100 tests of the removed truck modules go. 27 tests come in: `model_solid_ranges` 4, kernel `machining_mesh_open` 6, kernel lib `step_face_winding` 2, kernel `machining_mesh_bounds` 1, geometry `step_metre_unit` 1, `shared_edge` 3, `winding_align` 2, geometry `step_twisted_flank` 2, app `import_step_twisted_flank` 2, `bore_facet_sagitta` 1, `step_chord_units` 1, `lead_approach` 1, `unreached` 1. Ignored: 120 -> 125 (6 known-fail markers in, 1 heavy-lane ignore out with its module).

## Gate

- Batch gate on bc5daa32d: 951 steps, 0 failed, clippy clean.
- Targeted runs on the final head 2ad350627 (debug, `-j 12`):
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test step_twisted_flank`: 2 passed.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import_step_twisted_flank`: 2 passed.
  - `--test bore_facet_sagitta`: 3 passed. `--test step_chord_units`: 4 passed.
  - `--test winding_align`: 10 passed, 1 ignored (#2845). `--test import_step_outward`: 3 passed.

## Follow-ups

title: fix(motion): turning rides keep no sample closer than half the chord share
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`: a new private step `thin` runs after the bisection in `profile_offset` and `profile_offset_in`.
- `thin` drops each sample that is closer than half the chord share (`MIN_GAP_SHARE = 0.5`) to the last kept sample.
- The first and the last sample (the window ends) always stay. At the end, a kept sample that is too near the last sample gives way to it.
- Each kept sample is an exact point of the offset curve. No new point is made.
- A chord moves by at most two gaps (one share). The callers pass a quarter of the user tolerance as the share, so the ride stays within half of the user tolerance.
- The module doc now states this bound.

## Cause

The bisection (`settle`) halves the interval toward a vertical tangent of the offset curve. The samples come closer than 1 micrometre. Exact float twins of candidate stations also occur (a gap of 1e-16 mm). `out.dedup()` removes only exactly equal samples. The lathe posts wrote these runs as identical `G01` blocks.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_spacing.rs`:

- `od_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped bar and the collar, tol 1e-2, 2.5e-3 and 1e-4.
- `id_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped hole wall.
- `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap`: the window ends 1e-7 past a candidate station. This pins the give-way at the end.
- `thinning_keeps_the_window_ends_and_the_nose`: the ends stay, and each sample is at distance d from the profile.
- `thinned_chords_stay_within_the_bound`: 9 points on each chord stand at least `d - 2 * tol` from the profile.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged `offset.rs` the OD and ID spacing pins fail with `gap 0.00000000000000044` (OD) and `gap 0.00000000000000011` (ID).

Mutations:

- The old `offset.rs`: 2 pins red. Restored: green.
- The tail give-way disabled (`while ... && false`): `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap` red (`gap 0.0000001`). Restored: green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion lib, turning_bore, turning_offset_spacing, turning_prof).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Also green by hand: motion `turning_contour`, `turning_contour_stock`. App debug: 25 lathe and turning binaries (`lathe_post*`, `turning*`, `sim_lathe_body`, `coarse_laws`, `project_roundtrip` and others).
- Release `--ignored` on 16 app lathe and turning binaries: green (1 heavy test in that set).

## Goldens moved

4 files. Each diff only removes lines (516 removed, 0 added):

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_mm.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_inch.nc` (-129)

Most removed lines are runs of identical blocks, for example 40 x `G01 X7. Z2. F0.04` and 39 x `G01 X9.1 Z3.05 F0.05`. The other removed lines are sub-gap steps at the start of the same face, for example `Z2.001` to `Z2.005`. The goldens were made again with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Not exercised

- The full heavy reach (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base main`, 223 app lanes) did not run. The author must run it on the final head before the PR is flagged ready.
- The cone-thread example of #2394 is not on main. It was not posted again.
- At a very small user tolerance (for example 0.001 mm) the gap is less than the posted resolution. Two rounded blocks can then still be equal. This costs no position.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `offset.rs` or the new test file.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2882-ride-min-spacing.md`. The post-side alternative (drop a repeated block in each lathe post) was dropped.

Written by an Opus lead + Haiku workers (lane trial). The workers wrote about 85% of the lines: `thin` and its call sites, the first four pins, and the decision record. The lead wrote about 15%: the chord-bound correction (1.5x to 2x share, because the give-way at the end can double the gap), the tail pin, the clippy fix, the golden refresh and the review.

Effort: high

Changelog: Turning profile rides no longer post runs of identical G01 blocks: samples closer than half the chord share are dropped.

title: fix(2d): refuse a no-pick chamfer on a partly bevelled edge loop by name
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer with no picks now refuses at generation when a top edge loop carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length.
The message names a point on the bevelled part and a point on the sharp part. It asks the user to pick the edges.

Example text, from the unit test fixture: `the edge loop near X1.000 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length - it is sharp near X30.500 Y0.000 - a chamfer with no picks would cut the sharp part; pick the edges to break`.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`: the new function `partly_bevelled`, and one call in `ride_loops`.
- `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs`: the plate of the issue, with and without the extra vertex.
- `docs/decisions/2887-chamfer-partly-bevelled.md`: the decision record.

The issue permits two results: a ride of the bevelled segments only, or a named refusal that asks for picks. This PR takes the refusal.

## Cause

`ride_loops` classified each top loop whole, by the farthest vertex from the wall loop.
A loop that is bevelled on one side has two readings.
With an extra vertex on the top edge of the bevel, the loop read as bevelled. The ride then cut the three sharp sides.
Without that vertex, the two bevel corners lie on the wall, and the loop read as sharp. The tip then stood inside the part at the bevel.
The verifier refused the two programs as a gouge at a coordinate, with no reason.

## The check

The check runs for each segment of the matched top loop. It measures the two ends and the middle against the wall loop.

- A segment within 1e-6 mm of the wall is sharp.
- A segment more than 0.05 mm from the wall is bevelled.
- A segment between the two values counts as neither.

The loop is refused when it has a bevelled segment and more than one chamfer width of sharp length.
The result does not depend on tessellation.

## Tests

Pins:

- `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_a_plate_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name` (app, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`)
- `the_refusal_does_not_depend_on_an_extra_vertex_on_the_bevel` (app, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name` (motion lib)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_with_an_extra_vertex_too` (motion lib)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_all_round_is_not_partly_bevelled` (motion lib)

Mutation: with `chamfer_ride.rs` of `upstream/main` 17b1b2b81, the two app pins fail (`a partly bevelled edge loop with no picks is refused: ()`: generation succeeds). With the fix, the two pins pass.
The motion unit pins were not run against the old file: they call the new function, so the old file does not compile with them.

Unchanged and green: the six older `chamfer_ride` unit tests and the seven tests of `chamfer_modelled_edge` (#303, #2435, #2596).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 7991bc04b (4 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Heavy review results

Verified head: `7991bc04bba6db467460b375821a8ea30011786d`. No source changes were needed for the review finding.

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed: 223 steps, 0 failed, 47.6 minutes.

- Release build: passed (1 step).
- Motion heavy lane: passed (34 steps). Tests: 56 passed. Two registered failures for #1950 failed as expected.
- App heavy lane: passed (188 steps). Tests: 42 passed. One registered failure for #1950 failed as expected.
- No unexpected failure occurred. No golden file changed.

The three registered #1950 cases are:

- Motion: `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`.
- Motion: `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`.
- App: `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 4 steps, 0 failed, 11.9 minutes.
Motion lib: 477 passed, 10 ignored. `chamfer_modelled_edge`: 7 passed. `chamfer_partly_bevelled`: 2 passed.

`cargo clippy -j 32 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

The heavy run started with `upstream/main` at `0510ff382015bfb46f088c44436919c0b000de58`.
The quick run started with that ref at `7173bb44ac16512c1571fc58b804816e98712e68` after an external fetch.
Both bases give merge base `17b1b2b81c2fc555fdaa3f06dec73000d19d20c7` and the same three changed files.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes.

## Not exercised

- A partial ride of only the bevelled segments is not in this PR. The decision record gives the reasons.
- No note lists whole loops that a no-pick chamfer leaves sharp (the #2596 case). `ride_loops` has no warning channel. That is separate work.
- Curved partly bevelled loops (a fillet on a part of an arc) have no test. The check uses three samples for each segment.
- The verifier is not changed.

## Overlaps

`chamfer_ride.rs`: no open PR changes it.
#2831 adds a field to `OpParams::Face` in each test file that builds it. The new test file here builds `OpParams::Face` too. The PR that merges second adds the field in `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs`.

The lead wrote the guard again from the worker's reported diff, with small changes (`hypot`, an iterator loop, a shared fixture for the unit tests). - Worker 3 (Haiku) wrote the decision record (26 lines) from the lead's content. The lead did not change it.
- In lines: workers 171 of 264 (65 %), lead 93 of 264 (35 %). The root cause, the design and the review are the lead's.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer with no picks on an edge loop that has a modelled chamfer on only part of its length now refuses by name and asks for picks; before, the post gate refused it as a gouge with no reason (#2887).

title: feat(drilling): fine boring cycle (G76) with a required shift
body:
Stacked on #2823 (merge #2823 first).

## What changed

Fine boring is a new cycle on the drilling operation. This is the last slice of #1445, and it is the work of #1479.

- `CycleChoice::FineBore { shift_x_um, shift_y_um }` is a new cycle choice. The shift is a required part of the choice. There is no default shift.
- `CycleKind::FineBore` is a new CL cycle kind. The `.cl` text writes `FineBore`. The `.cnc` stream writes `CYCLE FINEBORE`.
- The chain of one hole is: feed in, shift at the bottom, rapid out at the shifted XY, shift back at R.
- The post engine reads the shift from the chain. It gives the shift to the script as `ShiftX` and `ShiftY`.
- The post engine refuses the cycle by name for a script that does not declare `fineBoring = true`.
- The Haas post declares `fineBoring`. It writes `G76 X Y Z R I J P F`, one whole block for each hole. It never writes `Q`.
- Each of the other 17 shipped posts refuses the cycle by name.
- A machine file can state `spindle.orientation`. The value `false` refuses a fine bore with any post.
- The generator refuses a shift that the bar has no room for. The room is `(tool dia. - shank dia.) / 2`.
- The commands refuse a zero shift, a shift above 5 mm on one axis, and a shift that is not smaller than a hole radius.
- The verifier reads the three stopped-spindle rapids with the stopped bar. It still reads the shank and the holder at the shifted position.
- The reach law holds a fine bore to the shank fit in the hole, as it does for a bore and a ream.
- The project file, MCP `edit_operation` and the Cycle combo of the drill page carry the choice and its shift.

A program that does not choose the cycle posts the same bytes as before.

## Cause

Hole making had no fine boring cycle. A bore cycle rapids out with the tip on the wall, and the tip marks the finished bore.

## Design

- The shift is in the chain, not in a new record field. The posted `I` and `J` are the shift of the chain, so the two cannot disagree. The WCS flip, the WCS yaw and the axis mirror already transform the moves and the cycle centre together.
- The refusal for a post is in the engine. A new post is refused until it declares the flag.
- Haas `G76` reads `I` and `J` as the shift along X and Y. The `Q` form takes its direction from Setting 27. A program cannot state that setting, so the post never writes `Q`.
- Fanuc, Mazak and Doosan take the direction of `Q` from a control parameter. These posts refuse. #2886 has the work for these controls, for Heidenhain `CYCL DEF 202`, for Sinumerik `CYCLE86` and for Mach4.
- The verifier models the tool as the cylinder that the turning edge sweeps. That cylinder, shifted by `s`, enters the bore wall by `s`. With the spindle stopped, the bar reaches `bar radius + s` from the hole axis and the tip reaches `tool radius - s`. The two stay inside the cylinder that the feed in cut while `s < tool radius - bar radius`. The feed in was read over the same cylinder.
- The shank and the holder are not inside that cylinder. The solid law reads them at the shifted position.
- `docs/decisions/1445-fine-boring.md` has the options that were dropped.

MCP: `edit_operation` takes `"cycle": {"fine_bore": {"shift_x": 0.3, "shift_y": -0.4}}` (millimetres). The word `"fine_bore"` with no shift is refused.

## Tests

Pins:

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `drilling::tests_fine_bore` (6 tests): the chain, the choice with no default, the room door, the bore door.
- `camcraft-post`, `fine_bore_cycle` (8 tests): the stream word, the Haas `G76` block, the `P0` word, the refusal with no shift, the refusal of each other post, the machine gate, the file word, the golden.
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::fine_bore` (4 tests): the acquittal, the cases that keep each conviction, the holder that is still read.
- `camcraft-app`, `fine_bore_cycle` (9 tests): the command with undo and redo, the project file, the `.cl` text, the stamp, the command doors, the generator door, the shank fit, the Haas post, the machine gate, the post refusal, MCP.
- `camcraft-ui` lib, `egui_app::tests::cycle_combo` (3 tests) and `egui_app::tests::holes_fine_bore` (2 tests).

Red before the change: the pins do not compile on the base. `CycleChoice::fine_bore`, `CycleKind::FineBore` and `fine_bore_gate` do not exist there. This is a new cycle, so there is no old behaviour to show red at run time. The first run of the app pin on the new generator, before the verifier change, was red:

```text
the verifier accepts the shifted retract: [RapidInStock { at: 2 }, RapidInStock { at: 3 }]
post blocked - 2 warning(s): FineBore1: rapid move 2 travels through stock ...; FineBore1: rapid move 3 travels through stock ...
```

Mutations. Each one was red with the guard removed and green after the restore:

| Guard removed | Pin that went red |
|---|---|
| motion: the room door (`s >= room`) | `a_shift_the_bar_has_no_room_for_is_refused_by_name` |
| motion: the zero shift at the choice | `the_fine_bore_choice_has_no_default_shift` |
| motion: the zero shift at the generator | `a_hand_made_zero_shift_is_refused_by_the_generator` |
| motion: the rapid out put back on the hole axis | `fine_bore_shifts_off_the_wall_before_the_rapid_out` |
| post engine: the `fineBoring` gate | `every_other_post_refuses_a_fine_bore_by_name` |
| post engine: the refusal with no shift | `a_fine_bore_with_no_shift_in_its_chain_is_refused_by_name` |
| Haas: the refusal with no shift | `a_fine_bore_with_no_shift_in_its_chain_is_refused_by_name` |
| Haas: the chain suppression at the shifted XY | `haas_writes_g76_with_the_shift_of_the_chain` |
| Haas: the `I` and `J` words | `haas_writes_g76_with_the_shift_of_the_chain` |
| machine: `fine_bore_gate` | `a_machine_that_cannot_stop_oriented_refuses_a_fine_bore` |
| machine: `spindle.orientation` must be a boolean | `spindle_orientation_must_be_a_boolean_or_the_file_is_refused` |
| verifier: the room in the acquittal | `a_shift_with_no_room_for_the_bar_keeps_every_conviction` |
| verifier: the chain shape in the acquittal | `a_group_that_is_not_the_cycles_chain_keeps_every_conviction` |
| verifier: the holder reading in the solid law | `the_solid_law_skips_the_stopped_edge_and_still_reads_the_shifted_holder` |
| verifier: the acquittal call in law (d) | `fine_bore_is_an_undoable_drill_parameter_that_generates_the_shift_and_round_trips` |
| app: the door in `CreateOperation` | `a_fine_bore_with_no_usable_shift_is_refused_when_the_command_is_made` |
| app: the door in `EditOperationParams` | `a_fine_bore_with_no_usable_shift_is_refused_when_the_command_is_made` |
| app: the shift in the digest | `the_shift_is_in_the_operation_stamp` |
| app: the machine gate call | `a_fine_bore_on_a_machine_that_cannot_stop_oriented_is_refused_by_name` |
| app: the fine bore in the shank-fit list of the reach law | `a_fine_bore_is_held_to_the_shank_fit_not_to_the_flute` |

Gate on head `fd5767af0`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 936 steps, 0 failed, 61.8 minutes. The diff touches the shared `cl` crate, so the quick tier ran as the batch tier: each debug suite of geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui, and clippy.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean.

## Goldens moved

One new golden: `crates/post/tests/golden/fine_bore/haas.nc`. No existing `.nc` or `.cl` file changed (`git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` lists this file only).

The cycle lines of the new golden:

```text
G99
G76 X10. Y10. Z-12. R2. I0.3 J-0.4 P500 F60
G80
```

## Not exercised

- No literature search ran. The session had no web access. No manual page was read in this session. Check the Haas `G76` block (`I`, `J`, `P`) against the Haas Mill Operator's Manual before a real cut.
- Nothing ran on a real control.
- No heavy lane ran (`cargo xtask gate heavy`). The diff reaches the motion, sim and app heavy lanes. Run it before this PR is flagged ready.
- The posted shift under a WCS flip, a WCS yaw or an inverted axis has no test of its own. The shift is read from moves that these transforms already change.
- Inch output of `I` and `J` has no test.
- The tip direction is the statement of the user. No test or check can prove it.
- The Machines sheet has no row for `spindle.orientation`. No shipped machine file states it (#2886).
- The UI was not started. The two UI tests drive the page in the test harness.
- A fine bore with the holder near a wall is read by the solid law only (the part). The fixture laws read the holder at the chain positions as before, and have no fine bore test.

## Overlaps

- #2823 changes the same function, `camcraft_motion::drilling::cycle::drill` (the Back bore arm and the dwell list). This PR is stacked on it and adds the fine bore arm and one entry in the same dwell list.
- #2831, #2833, #2836, #2716 and #2714 change `crates/app/src/project/params.rs` and `params_impl.rs` in other operation kinds. #2821 and #2024 change `crates/app/src/project/entity.rs` in other types. #2763 changes `crates/sim/src/sim.rs`, which this PR does not change. Each touches the same file, a different function. The PR that merges second takes a refresh.
- #2646, #2515 and #2506 add new posts. They do not declare `fineBoring`, so the engine refuses a fine bore for them with no change.

Effort: high

Changelog: Drilling has a fine boring cycle (G76 on Haas) with a required shift off the wall; other posts refuse it by name, and a machine that cannot stop its spindle oriented refuses it.

Fixes #1479
Fixes #1445

title: fix(post): refuse Fanuc G76 when the start point is above material
body:
## What changed

- Added `start_in_air: bool` to `cl::ThreadCycle` and `ThreadCycleDto` (defaults to `false`).
- Added optional `AIR 1` flag to `THREAD` records in `crates/post/src/post/cnc_thread.rs` and exposed it to post scripts as `properties.StartInAir`.
- Refused G76 by name in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`g76Why`) whenever `p.StartInAir !== true`.
- Added `cycle_infeed_band` and `part_band_clear` in `crates/motion/src/turning/thread_cycle.rs` to check the full rapid-infeed axial band `[min(start_s, s_deep) - insert_width/2, max(start_s, s_deep) + insert_width/2]` against the part silhouette and raw stock.
- Added `crates/app/src/operation/g76_start.rs` to refine `start_in_air` against the revolved part, stock and prior cuts. `TurnedAhead` now carries the grooving blade half-width `band`.
- Replaced isolated stock samples with continuous coverage checks after review. Each interval between stock profile breakpoints has a conservative bound above the root. Prior cuts must cover the full bound. Bounded subdivision checks coverage from several cuts. The check refuses G76 when it cannot prove clearance.
- Reduced blade and nose credit by the clearance margin. Blade credit follows the actual swept segment. The check also proves coverage between radial samples. It does not credit uncertain stock holes.
- Updated `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs` and `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs` so a threading pass can start in free air in front of a free end face without false out-of-domain rest warnings.
- Updated the Fanuc G76 test bar fixtures and three golden `.nc` files to start in free air (`Z16.` / `Z16.625` / `Z0.6299`) instead of inside a solid `Z=40` bar.
- Moved the clearance algorithm to `crates/motion/src/turning/g76_clearance.rs`. The public API takes cut and pilot values.
- Kept stock breakpoints and document integration in `app`. Moved the radial-gap and diagonal-blade tests to the motion crate.
- Recorded the design choice in `docs/decisions/2878-fanuc-g76-start-in-air.md`.

## Cause

A Fanuc-type G76 cycle moves the insert from the start point to each pass depth at rapid traverse. Previously, `fanuc-lathe.cps` emitted G76 without checking whether the start point stood in free air, and `turning::thread` clamped pass starts to the part silhouette domain. As a result, G76 started inside solid material (for example at `Z77.4` inside a `Z=78` end face on the cone-thread part).

## Tests

### Pinning tests (red before fix, green after fix)

- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_when_start_point_is_inside_a_solid_bar` (G76 refused by name, G32 still posts)
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_on_cone_thread_start_inside_end_face` (reproduces #2878 cone-thread part)
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_posts_when_start_point_is_in_free_air_in_front_of_end_face`
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_uncut_stock_in_front_of_end_face_and_posts_after_facing`
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_legacy_stream_without_air_flag`
- `camcraft-app::operation::g76_start::tests::relief_groove_wider_than_insert_passes_when_grooved_and_refuses_when_uncut_or_narrow`
- `camcraft-app::operation::g76_start::tests::flank_infeed_refuses_when_deep_pass_overlaps_end_face`
- `turning_thread_cycle::start_in_air_distinguishes_solid_bar_from_free_end_start`
- `operation::g76_start::tests::narrow_stock_rib_between_old_stations_refuses` pins the reviewer's narrow rib between axial samples.
- `turning_g76_clearance::radial_gap_between_prior_cut_capsules_refuses` pins a radial gap and permits cuts with a safe overlap.
- `turning_g76_clearance::diagonal_blade_does_not_credit_its_deep_tip_across_the_whole_band` pins the actual blade sweep.

- `turning_g76_clearance::pilot_values_prove_only_the_removed_cone` pins the motion API for pilot dimensions and cone coverage.

### Earlier mutation checks

- Removed `p.StartInAir !== true` guard in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`: 4 of 5 tests in `lathe_post_g76_start` failed (red), then passed after restore (green).
- Disabled `g76_start::judge` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: `g76_refuses_uncut_stock_in_front_of_end_face_and_posts_after_facing` failed (red), then passed after restore (green).
- Restored post-retain `lat.push(w0); lat.push(w1);` in `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`: `g76_posts_when_start_point_is_in_free_air_in_front_of_end_face` failed with `6.0000 mm rest` (red), then passed after restore (green).
- Forced `start_in_air = true` in `crates/motion/src/turning/thread_cycle.rs`: `start_in_air_distinguishes_solid_bar_from_free_end_start` failed (red), then passed after restore (green).

- Review fix mutation: restored the sampled production checks while keeping the new tests. All three new regression tests failed (RED). Restored the continuous checks: all five `operation::g76_start::tests` passed (GREEN).

### Earlier gate and clippy results

These results apply to the previous head, before the domain move.

- Previous head: `41ce5778c17a886edf7288bf4db544ce4e5b1d04`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` fell back to batch because `crates/cl` changed. The full run completed 955 steps in 36.6 minutes. Only clippy failed. A minimal guard change fixed that lint. On that head, all five clearance pins passed. The failed-only clippy rerun passed: 1 step, 0 failed, 37 seconds.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on that head: 2 minutes 58 seconds, 0 warnings.
