title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |
| `params`: the allowance in the stamp | same | red |
| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |
| project: the key is read | `mcp_sets_the_group_...` | red |
| motion: entered mode refused (`Guards::source`) | `each_guard_is_pinned_...` | red |
| motion: no stock refused (`Guards::stock`) | same | red |
| motion: the allowance grows the material (`Guards::allowance`) | same | red |
| motion: the film of the reading (one cell diagonal put back) | same | red |

The three motion guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior_adaptive::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off.
The first run of the two stamp mutants and of the bad-value mutant stayed green on the app tests, because another path gave the same result. I added the two lib pins for them, and the mutants are red on those pins.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 3914606bf: green, 359 steps, 0 failed (55.5 min). The diff against `upstream/main` holds #2822 too, so its suites ran. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat base-2822 HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.
The diff against `upstream/main` shows 3 deleted `.nc` files under `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/`. The base (#2822, head 8040ea771) does not have them yet. This PR does not touch them. A merge of main brings them back.

## Not exercised

- The rows of the group on the 2D Adaptive page. The page keeps the value of the draft and shows no rows. Follow-up: #2884.
- The MCP skill row. The session could not write `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. Follow-up, with the row text: #2885.
- A golden CL file for the rest pass of the 2D Adaptive. The tests read the path against a simulation.
- A setup whose stock is carried from an earlier setup, a WCS yaw, and the field stock engine. The code path is that of #2822, which has the same limits.
- Islands and a neck in the app job. The motion suite of #2031 covers them on a proved stock, not on the column stock.
- Stock to leave on this operation together with the group.
- The toolpath on a machine.
- Linux only; debug build. The app was not started by hand.

## Known limits (recorded in `docs/decisions/1446-rest-adaptive-op.md`)

- Real residue thinner than the film (2.4 cells) along a wall is not cut.
- The `entry` field and the links of the operation are not read with the group on. Each entry is a plunge into proved-clear space.
- #2032 (entry with clearance proved for the full cutter, on the 2D Pocket) stays open and is not part of this PR.

## Literature

- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", LNCS 500, Springer, 1991.
- Z. Yao, S. K. Gupta, D. S. Nau, "Algorithms for selecting cutters in multi-part milling problems", Computer-Aided Design 35(9), 2003.

These sources describe pocket geometry and cutter coverage. The stock-proof rules are the decision of this project. No code or text of a different CAM product was read or used.

## Overlaps

- #2822 (base of this stack): `rest_op.rs` (`rest_of`, `rest_refusal`, `reads_previous_ops`), `job.rs` (the previous-operations arm), `params.rs`, `generate.rs`.
- #2842 changes the level ladder lines in `adaptive::rest::guarded`. This PR moves those two lines into `adaptive::rest_levels`. It is the same code. The PR that merges second applies the step of #2842 in `rest_levels`.
- #2833 and #2831 add fields to the pocket family. They touch the same constructor lists of `OpParams::Adaptive2D` (the kinds seed, the project mapping, seven test files). Each side adds lines. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2853, #2817, #2836, #2716, #2714, #2678 touch the same files in different functions. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: The 2D Adaptive operation has rest machining from the previous operations: it cuts only what the earlier operations of the setup left, and each plunge stands where their stock proves the cutter clear (set through MCP or the project file; the page rows follow in #2884).

title: fix(turning): allow threading passes to start in front of the end face
body:
## What changed

- Removed the post-filter push of `w0` and `w1` in `revolve::lattice` (`crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`). Every in-domain band endpoint is already in `lat`. Removing those four lines keeps `lat` strictly inside `[d_lo, d_hi]`. Free air past an end face no longer creates intervals where the scan reads `E(s) = 0` as rest.
- Computed `k_hi` in `thread_planned_in` (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`) from the unclamped `f.station_of(p.top_z)`. Kept `s_lo..=s_hi` clamped to `[d_lo, d_hi]` for `ref_top`, valley phase discovery, and the empty-window refusal. A threading pass can now start in free air in front of the end face.
- Added `crates/motion/tests/turning_thread_end_face.rs` with four pinning tests.
- Added `docs/decisions/2879-thread-free-air-start.md`.

## Cause

Two defects prevented a free-end thread from starting in front of the end face:

1. `revolve::lattice` filtered `lat` to `[d_lo, d_hi]` and then pushed `w0` and `w1` back into `lat`. Whenever a move band extended past `d_hi` (by 0.1 mm on a free-end groove, or by whole pitches on a free-air lead-in), `revolve::scan` evaluated an air interval where `E(s) = 0` and reported the capped wave floor (5.0 mm) as rest.
2. `blade::setup` clamped `s_hi` to `d_hi`, and `thread_planned_in` used that clamped `s_hi` in `k_hi`. Setting `top_z` in front of the end face (such as Z81 for a Z78 end face) still started each pass inside the bar at Z77.5.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/turning_thread_end_face.rs`:

- `free_end_groove_band_past_end_face_is_not_rest`: red before fix (`rest_mm: 5.000000000000001`), green after fix.
- `free_air_lead_in_starts_in_front_of_end_face_and_judges_clean`: red before fix (started at `77.5` instead of `80.5`), green after fix.
- `free_air_start_still_convicts_real_gouge_and_real_rest_on_part`: checks overcut, shallow cut, missed turn, and a free-air lattice point whose flank clips a solid end face.
- `groove_at_free_end_face_spilling_into_end_air_is_not_rest`: red before fix (`rest_mm: 4.0`), green after fix.

Mutation checks on `turning_thread_end_face`:

- Reverted `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (3 of 4 failed with `rest_mm: 5.0` and `rest_mm: 4.0`). Restored: green.
- Reverted `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (`free_air_lead_in_starts_in_front_of_end_face_and_judges_clean` failed: `got 77.5`). Restored: green.

Gates:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (10 steps, 0 failed: `motion build`, `lib`, `turning_blade`, `turning_coarse`, `turning_stock`, `turning_thread`, `turning_thread_cycle`, `turning_thread_dips`, `turning_thread_end_face`, `turning_thread_infeed`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Final-head verification for the review finding (2026-11-20):

- Head: `5de53b78267abc3f10eaac8b749f9e7ff81975f9` (unchanged). The review requested missing test evidence. No source or test changed.
- Base: `upstream/main` at `3ffe2338f775b2f254524f5f8e642aae5181aebb`.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: passed, 220 steps, 0 failed, 144.2 minutes.
- Motion heavy lane: passed, 34 steps. All 56 ordinary heavy tests passed. Both declared known-failure checks for #1950 matched their expected failures.
- App heavy lane: passed, 185 steps. All 42 heavy tests passed.
- The combined release build accounts for the remaining step. Selected targets with no ignored tests completed without failures.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed, 10 steps, 0 failed, 32.6 minutes. Motion library: 468 passed, 10 ignored. All eight selected turning suites passed, including all four `turning_thread_end_face` tests.
- `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed, no warnings, 2 minutes 2 seconds.
- These results use the unchanged PR head. The review used a trial merge with main, so its library test count differs.
- No new mutation check applies to this evidence-only update. The existing mutation results above were independently repeated in the latest review.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- No app-level end-to-end Fanuc G76 post run (tracked in #2878).
- No UI test or physical machine run.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR touches `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`, `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`, or `crates/motion/tests/turning_thread_end_face.rs`.

title: feat(catalog): add the turning case cone-thread - a cone with a threaded end
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the example catalog case `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread`.
The case is a spun turning profile: a cone with a threaded end.

- The stock is a 30 mm bar, 79 mm long.
- The part has a collar, a 20 mm to 10 mm cone over 40 mm, an 8 mm neck and an M10x1.5 thread, 15 mm long.
- The machine is the built-in `Lathe` (`assets/machines/lathe.mch`). The post is `Fanuc Lathe`.
- The program has six operations: `Face`, `Rough profile`, `Finish profile`, `Neck`, `Thread`, `Part off`.

The case folder has the layout of #2393:

- `model/gen_cone_thread_obj.py` and its two meshes
- `build.camscript`
- `cone-thread.camproj`
- `cone-thread.nc`
- `README.md`, which walks through the steps

The PR also adds one test to `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` and the decision file `docs/decisions/2394-cone-thread.md`.
No file in `crates/*/src` changes.

## Cause

Issue #2394 asks for this case. The catalog infrastructure of #2393 is on `main` since v0.24.0.

## Decisions that differ from the issue text

The decision file gives each one with its reason.

- The case imports two models: the turned blank and the finished part. Profile Finish cannot finish the model that the Threading operation needs (#2880).
- The neck needs a sixth operation, a Groove Finish. The issue lists five.
- The thread posts as G32 passes, not as the G76 cycle. A G76 cycle would start inside the part (#2878, #2879).
- The threading insert is a tool definition in the script. No catalog insert fits a 1.5 mm pitch (#893).
- The shoulder has no fillet (#2881).

## Bugs filed on the way

The issue says: "Any refusal or wrong output found on the way is filed as its own bug and linked here."

- #2878 (`P1`): a G76 cycle starts inside the part.
- #2879 (`P3`): a threading pass cannot start in front of the end face.
- #2880 (`P3`): Profile Finish reads thread valleys and a neck step as rest.
- #2881 (`P3`): a steep fillet chord sends the profile ride far out of the bar.
- #2882 (`P3`): the profile rides post runs of identical `G01` blocks. The committed program has 408 such blocks.

## Tests

Pin: `example_catalog::turning_cone_thread_case_posts_the_taper_and_the_thread`. It reads the committed program and asserts:

- the operation order,
- the slope of each finish block on the cone (10 mm of diameter over 40 mm),
- the G32 passes at lead 1.5, the last pass at the 8.16 mm root, the pass end at Z63.9,
- the neck plunge to X8 and the part-off to X0.

The two suite tests that iterate all cases also cover the new case: `every_catalog_case_opens_regenerates_verifies_and_posts_byte_for_byte` and `every_catalog_case_rebuilds_from_camscript`.

Red first: without the case folder the pin fails with `catalog case turning/cone-thread is missing`.

Mutations of the committed `.nc`, each restored after the run:

| Mutation | Pin |
|---|---|
| case folder removed | red |
| `G01 X10.212 Z58.4` changed to `X12.212` (taper) | red: `is off the taper: -0.141` |
| `G32 Z63.9 F1.5` changed to `Z65.4` (thread end) | red: `each pass ends at the neck, Z63.9` |
| files restored | green |

The first form of the taper assert let the taper mutation pass. The assert now checks each block on the cone.

Gates on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`app:example_catalog`, whole suite, 16 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check`: `checked 2d/first-part`, `checked turning/cone-thread`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: the diff reaches no heavy lane.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows one new file, `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc` (1197 lines). No file under `tests/golden/` changes.

## Not exercised

- No machine or control simulator ran the program.
- The lathe stock simulation does not cut threads. The verify verdict says so, and the thread is judged by its own operation verdict.
- The tool holders are not judged: the tools have no modelled body.
- `cargo xtask catalog --screenshots` and `--pdf` did not run.
- The UI did not open the project.

## Notes for the review

- `cone-thread.camproj` is 1.5 MB. The seed case is 0.2 MB. The project holds two meshes and the toolpaths.
- When #2882 is fixed, the committed `.nc` changes. That PR must rebuild the case.

## Overlaps

#2877 (draft, case `2d/contour-tabs`) touches the same file, `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`, in a different function. The two PRs each add a new test function at the end of the file. Whichever merges second refreshes and keeps the two functions. The case folders do not overlap.

Changelog: Examples: the catalog case `turning/cone-thread` shows a lathe job - a cone with an M10x1.5 threaded end (face, rough and finish profile, neck groove, thread, part-off) on the Fanuc lathe post.

body:
## What changed

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings.rs`: The tool page in Properties now owns `tool_page_scroll`. It keeps `Apply` or `Add tool` beside `Close` in a fixed bottom footer.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`: `tool_shape_editor_window` reserves footer height and displays `ErrorScope::Tool` messages above `Close`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings_grid.rs`: `Tool number` drops `(0 = next free)` from its label and puts that hint in `prop_row_hint`. `Material group`, `Holder diameter`, and `Holder length` gain hover hints.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_page.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_lathe_page.rs`: Body tab state lines replace `body:`, `draft:`, `placed:`, `placement:`, and `judged` with plain sentences (`In use:`, `Ready to apply:`, `Placed from`, `Placed:`, `Placement error:`). `Tool axis`, `Tip offset`, and `Body frame` use label-left `prop_row` or `prop_row_hint` rows.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_holder_picker.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs`: `Library holder`, `Gauge length`, and `Projection` align label-left with `num_row` fields. `editor` calls `state.sync_tool_profile_ui()` before it draws the picker.
- `docs/decisions/2007-tool-editor-footer-plain-state.md`: Records the design choices and the dropped scope.

## Cause

Earlier #2007 changes moved tool settings to Properties and moved shape controls into `Tool shape`, but two items remained open:

1. `tool_settings::page` ran inside the shared scroll area, so `Apply` and `Add tool` scrolled out of view on short viewports while `Close` stayed pinned below.
2. `Tool number`, the shape-window holder rows, the Body tab placement fields, and Body state lines still used raw labels or jargon. `tool_shape_editor_window` also did not display `ErrorScope::Tool` messages.

## Tests

title: fix(multiaxis): rotary operations read a face selection or refuse it
body:
## What changed

- Rotary Parallel keeps its cut over the picked faces. The kernel plans the raster on the full model, as before. Then it keeps each cut point where the line from the axis through the ball centre meets a picked facet. The radial relink builds the links between the kept pieces.
- The axis fit, the gouge laws and the verify still read the full model.
- Rotary Parallel refuses, by name, a selection that it cannot use:
  - a pick that is not a face;
  - picks on two models;
  - a face that does not look away from the axis (an end face, a bore wall);
  - picks that form separate groups;
  - picks that no pass lies over.
- Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset refuse a face selection by name. They do not cut the full model silently. Face containment for these two kinds is not in this PR: #2851 (Rotary Contour) and #2852 (Rotary Offset) hold that work.
- The generation stamp of a rotary operation with a selection gets a version mark. A path that was cached under the old reading becomes stale.
- An operation with no selection (source `Entity` or `Stock`) generates as before.

New files:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_pick.rs`: the clip, `faces_outward`, `groups`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rotary_picks.rs`: the picks read from the world, and the refusals.
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_face_selection.rs`: the pins.
- `docs/decisions/2848-rotary-face-selection.md`: the decision record.

## Cause

`material_of` reads a selection as the full facets of the picked models. The rotary arms of `run_job` gave those facets to the kernels. No code read which faces were picked, and no code refused the selection.

## Scope against the issue's "Done means"

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| Rotary Parallel accepts `SrcRef::Selection` | done |
| Rotary Contour, Rotary Offset accept `SrcRef::Selection` | not done: they refuse by name; #2851, #2852 |
| Toolpath stays in the picked faces | done for Rotary Parallel |
| Axis fit uses the full model | done, pinned |
| Stock simulation reads only the generated toolpath | no change necessary: the simulation reads the stored path |
| UI enables face selection for rotary operations | no change necessary: `SetOperationGeometry` has one door for all kinds (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`) |
| Unusable selections refuse with a clear message | done for all three kinds |
| Full-model operation is the same | done: the `None` path is the old code |
| Tests | done |

The maintainer's triage comment names the defect: the operation ignores the selection without a message. This PR removes that for all three kinds. If the maintainer wants the issue open until #2851 and #2852 merge, change `Fixes` to `Refs`.

## Tests

Pins (`crates/app/tests/rotary_face_selection.rs`), all red on `upstream/main` 326c938b1:

- `rotary_parallel_keeps_its_cut_over_the_picked_faces` - red before: "a cut at station -16 is off the picked neck (2..16)".
- `rotary_parallel_keeps_to_a_sector_and_still_turns_about_the_whole_models_axis`.
- `rotary_parallel_reads_a_welded_wall_pick_as_its_strips` - red before: "a cut at station -16.204 is off the picked patch".
- `rotary_parallel_refuses_a_selection_it_cannot_use_by_name` - red before: "the selection must be refused, not cut".
- `rotary_contour_and_offset_refuse_a_face_selection_by_name` - red before: "the selection must be refused, not cut".

Unit tests (`multiaxis::rotary_pick::tests`): the clip, `faces_outward`, `groups`.

Mutations (each was put in, the pins ran, the fix was put back):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| The two rotary arms of `generate.rs` as before the fix | 5 of 5 pins red |
| The kernel clip off (`rotary_parallel_over` ignores the picks) | 3 keep pins red |
| A chain pick read as "no facets" (no "is not a face" refusal) | refusal pin red |
| The `faces_outward` guard off | refusal pin red |
| The `groups` guard off | refusal pin red |

A file-level restore of `generate.rs` from `upstream/main` does not compile with the new job field. The arm-level mutation replaced it.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 294 steps, 0 failed, wall 25.2 min. `upstream/main` moved to 5fdbed9bd during the work, so the gate selected the suites of those new commits too. The branch base is 326c938b1; the new commits do not touch `crates/app/src/operation` or `crates/motion/src/multiaxis`.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The gate ran with the compile cache off (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`, no `RUSTC_WRAPPER`). The sccache server of this machine did not answer.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- The stamp version mark has no pin. A stamp under the old law cannot be made in a test.
- A WCS yaw (#760) with a face selection. The picks are facet indices, so they follow the turned material, but no test runs that pair.
- A part alignment (#326) with a face selection.
- The ramped infeed (`entry_ramp`) on clipped passes. The relink code is not changed, and its ramps are proved against the full part.
- A large sculpted pick (many thousands of facets): the time of the shadow test was not measured.
- No GUI run. No screenshot: the PR changes no UI code.
- The MCP `set_operation_geometry` door does not say the rotary refusals at the pick. Generation says them.

## Overlaps

Open PRs #2836, #2833, #2831, #2822, #2716, #2714 and #2678 change `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (and some change `job.rs` or `mod.rs`). They touch the same file, different arms of `run_job`. No open PR changes the rotary arms or `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Rotary Parallel keeps its passes to the picked faces; Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset refuse a face selection by name and no longer cut the full model silently (#2848).

Effort: high

Fixes #2848

title: fix(motion): the corner check reads a cusp loop that crosses itself
body:
## What changed

- `connected_pieces` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` reads each outer loop with `Region::from_slices`. Before, it used `Region::new`.
- A loop that crosses itself is now read as its even-odd lobes. The check does not stop.
- The noise filters of the check are the same (`PIECE_AREA_MIN`, `SLIVER_HALF_WIDTH`, `CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`).
- `docs/decisions/2849-corner-cusp-loop.md` records the decision.

This PR is partial work for #2849. It fixes the defect that the issue names ("loop crosses itself" in the corner check). It does not change the three toolpath tests of the issue.

## Cause

- `unreached_corners` computes `leftover = piece.difference(&swept)`. Then it calls `connected_pieces(&leftover)`.
- A bore drawn as chords leaves a cusp a few microns wide at each chord vertex.
- On the micron lattice, the boolean can return such a cusp as one loop that crosses itself.
- `Region::new` refuses that loop. The error stopped the whole corner check.
- The user then saw only the note "the check for corners of the stock tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself)".
- The defect does not need the solidcore importer. It is on `main` for a synthetic bore.

## Tests

Pin: `machining2d::unreached::law::a_chord_cusp_that_crosses_itself_does_not_stop_the_corner_check` (`camcraft-motion`, lib).

- The pin builds a 25 mm bore with 50, 60 and 63 chords. The reach is 2, 3 and 4 mm.
- It asserts that the check runs, names no corner and gives no note.
- On unchanged `upstream/main` (`326c938b1`) the pin fails: `50 chords, reach 2: invalid geometry: loop crosses itself`.
- Mutation: with `Region::new` put back, the pin is red. With `Region::from_slices`, the pin is green.

A probe sweep (not committed) used 24 to 400 chords, 9 reach values and 4 phases.

- Before the fix, 4726 of 13572 cases stopped with the error.
- After the fix, no case stops.
- After the fix, 36 cases name corners. Each has 24 to 28 chords and a reach of 8 or 10 mm. Their chord corners are larger than `CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on the final code.

- `motion lib`: ok.
- `app:adaptive_zero_margin_island`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main` shows one source file and one decision file.

## Not exercised

- The three tests of the issue with the solidcore mesh. PR B of #917 is not pushed, so the mesh is not available. The owner's diagnosis on the issue says that this fix does not change them.
- `Milling-test.step` through the solidcore reader. The pin uses a synthetic bore, not the real outline.
- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`). They did not run. They must run before this PR is flagged ready.
- A note that changes for a real project. A pocket that showed "did not run" can now show a corner note, or no note.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs`.

PR B of #917 marks the three tests with `known-fail #2849`. This PR does not close the issue, so those markers stay valid.

Changelog: The 2D pocket corner check no longer stops with "loop crosses itself" on a bore whose outline has fine chords.

Effort: high

Refs #2849

title: fix(kernel): machining-mesh parity for the solidcore STEP path
body:
## What changed

This PR is part B0 of #917. It prepares the kernel and the geometry crate for the solidcore STEP path. It does not switch the import.

- **Coordinate snap** (`crates/kernel/src/mesh_weld.rs`). Each coordinate snaps to a grid of 1e-3 mm when it is within 1e-9 mm of a grid point. The snap runs before the exact-bit weld. It gives +0.0, not -0.0. A triangle that the snap collapses is dropped. `sides()` refuses a mesh that the drop opened.
- **Turn an inward solid outward** (`machining_mesh.rs`). A watertight mesh with a negative volume gets its winding reversed. The mesh keeps a note: "the solid's faces all pointed inward (volume -X mm^3); the mesh is turned outward".
- **Refuse a breaking spline by name** (`crates/kernel/src/step_curve_guard.rs`). A pre-scan of the STEP exchange refuses an edge or swept spline that breaks the subdivision. The message names "edge" or "swept" and "subdivision".
- **Adaptive refinement with a cap** (`mesh_deviation.rs`). `measure_within` refines to depth 12, with a budget of 1<<21 samples. The bound `dmax + longest 3D side` is a rigorous upper bound (the distance to a set is 1-Lipschitz, and a mesh triangle is flat). `measure` keeps depth 3. The analytic distance moved to `mesh_distance.rs` to keep the file under 400 lines.
- **Solid ranges in the mesh** (`crates/geometry`). `Mesh.solids` holds one facet range for each solid. An empty list means one soup. `Mesh::from_solids` validates the ranges. `slice::slice_of` slices the full mesh first. On a non-manifold result with two or more ranges, it slices each range and unites the results. An inward range keeps the refusal. A range out of bounds gives `SliceError::Invalid`.
- Eight app tests use `Mesh::from_facets` instead of a struct literal, because `Mesh` has a new field.

The decision file is `docs/decisions/917-kernel-parity.md`.

## Changed pins

| Test | Old | New | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `machining_mesh` Solidcraft at 0.005 | replan: yes | replan: no (largest 0.0049999913) | the adaptive bound proves the first plan |
| `machining_mesh` Solidcraft at 0.1 | `largest() > 0.1`, replan: yes | `parametric > 0.1 && largest() <= 0.1`, replan: no (largest 0.0999999405) | the same |
| fillet_corner at 0.005 | refused | passes (largest 0.0049998025) | the same |

All other asserts stay. No tracked fixture replans now (checked: bspline_dome, spline_revolved, bar_cross_holes, fig8, twisted_flank, sample_ap214, Milling-test, modular_clamp_unit, Solidcraft from 0.002 to 0.2).

## Deviation

The snap pins are in `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_parity.rs`, not in `crates/geometry/tests`. `geometry::step` is not on main, and a geometry-to-kernel edge would be necessary. The decision file records this.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_parity.rs` (5 tests). These include: the noise goes; a point 1e-6 off a grid point stays; a collapsed facet is dropped; an inward solid turns outward.
- `crates/kernel/tests/step_curve_guard.rs` (4 tests).
- `crates/geometry/tests/mesh_solids.rs` (5 tests).
- `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh.rs` (7 tests, with the changed pins above).

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12): wall 46.8 min, 948 steps, 0 failed, clippy `-D warnings` ok.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main`: wall 64.6 min, 232 steps, 0 failed.

## Not exercised

- The app import still uses the old STEP path. The switch, the app part of the solid ranges and the import tests come in PR B (stacked on this PR).
- No GUI run.

Changelog: none (no user-visible change until PR B switches the import)

Refs #917

title: feat(motion): equal depth steps as an opt-in ladder parameter
body:
## What changed

- The default depth ladder does not change. It keeps the remainder in the last step. `top 20, bottom 2, stepdown 5` cuts `[15, 10, 5, 2]`.
- A new operation parameter, `equal_steps`, is in the `links.approach` object. The default is off.
- With `equal_steps` on, the ladder cuts the same number of levels in equal steps. The same example cuts `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
- `camcraft_motion::machining2d::equal_stepdown` gives the stepdown of the equal ladder. The level law `cut_levels_under` walks it. There is still one level law.
- `cut_levels_for(top, &approach, bottom, stepdown)` reads the mode and the stock top from the approach. These ladders call it: 2D Pocket (rings, adaptive, HSM, trochoidal, avoid), 2D Adaptive rest, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular (and its vault rings), 3D Pocket (plain, shell, rest refine).
- With stock above Top Z (#2004), the level at Top Z stays. The steps below it are equal.
- The project file writes `equal_steps` only when it is on. Older files load without a change.
- The params digest takes one byte only when the mode is on. The stamp of each existing operation does not change.
- The pocket region law of the app (`operation::area::ladder_planes`) reads the same mode through `OpParams::ladder_stepdown`. The region is built at the planes that the generator cuts.
- The Lead in / Lead out tab has one new row, "Equal depth steps", in the Linking group.
- `docs/decisions/2012-equal-steps.md` records the decision.

The parameter is undoable through `EditOperationParams`. The MCP `edit_operation` patch reaches it as `params.links.approach.equal_steps`. No new command and no new MCP tool are necessary.

## Cause

Issue #2012 asks for a decision between a remainder last step and equal steps. The level law had only the remainder ladder. The project rule "CAM choices are parameters" asks for a parameter with a default.

## Scope limit

Face, Trace, Engrave and Trochoidal Slot have no `links` object. They cannot save the parameter and keep the remainder ladder. Issue #2832 adds the parameter to them. Turning has its own infeed laws and is not part of this change.

## UI screenshots

The images show the Lead in / Lead out tab before and after the new row.
The before image uses the same merged scene with only the new row removed.
A temporary CPU renderer drew the real egui meshes, fonts and textures.
The test harness uses a placeholder viewport. The environment has no WGPU adapter.
No capture code or images are in the PR branch.

![Before: Linking group without Equal depth steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/d20bbdb08204c89873c18935732cf7039c10375c/pr-2842/leads-before.png)

![After: Linking group with Equal depth steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/d20bbdb08204c89873c18935732cf7039c10375c/pr-2842/leads-after.png)

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `the_default_ladder_keeps_the_remainder_and_equal_steps_is_opt_in`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_count_and_never_pass_the_stepdown`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_at_top_z_under_stock`
- `equal_steps_refuse_what_the_remainder_ladder_refuses`
- `a_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_pocket_with_keepouts_and_relief_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_trochoidal_adaptive_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_slot_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_bore_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_circular_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_3d_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`
- `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back`
- `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`
- `the_region_law_reads_the_stepdown_of_the_ladder_mode`
- `the_generated_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps`

Red before the change: yes. The motion pin did not compile on `upstream/main` 3970d3d03 (`Approach` has no field `equal_steps`; `cut_levels_for` and `equal_stepdown` do not exist).

Mutation results:

- Mutation 1: `ladder_stepdown` ignores the mode. Result: red. 10 of the 11 motion pins fail. The refusal pin stays green, which is correct.
- Mutation 2: the 12 caller files are the files of `upstream/main`, and the new law stays. Result: red. The 7 operation pins fail. The 4 law pins stay green.
- Mutation 3: the digest byte and the DTO write are removed. Result: red. `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`, `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back` and `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps` fail.
- After each mutation the code was restored and the pins were green again.

The first stamp pin did not fail in mutation 3. A default approach hashes no bytes, so each approach that is not the default already has a different stamp. The pin now also compares two approaches that are not the default.

Gate on the reviewed-finding fix:

- Head: `db53a0a827db8d3a59b518e1960f1f862198e0cd`. It merges `upstream/main` at `81407b31bab58d4037bbae90b18bbecfe9229103`.
- The merge conflict affected imports only. Both import sets stay. `pocket_avoid_with_relief` calls `cut_levels_for`.
- New pin: `a_pocket_with_keepouts_and_relief_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`. It checks both ladders with keep-outs and dogbone relief endpoints.
- Caller mutation: bypass `cut_levels_for`. The pin is RED on the equal cut planes. Restore: GREEN.
- Relief mutation: suppress corner relief. The pin is RED on the missing bottom relief endpoint. Restore: GREEN.
- Law mutation: ignore the equal mode. Eleven pins are RED. The refusal pin stays GREEN. Restore: all 12 motion pins GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. 163 of 164 steps pass in 22.8 minutes. Both motion and app `equal_steps` suites pass.
- The one failed step is `ui suites: lib`: 1,278 passed, seven failed, seven ignored. All seven failures report `No adapter found`.
- The explicit UI library rerun has the same result in 54.50 seconds. Neither run has a SIGSEGV.
- The seven failures are six `egui_app::report_tests` capture tests and `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds`. The environment exposes no WGPU adapter.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN on this head.
- The final worktree has no capture helper, review evidence or image files. The merge takes main's process version without a manual edit.

File length: `crates/motion/src/approach.rs` was 440 lines and is now 446. `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs` is now 402 lines.

## Latest review validation

Head: `db53a0a827db8d3a59b518e1960f1f862198e0cd` (unchanged). No source change was required by the latest review.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. 232 of 233 steps passed in 32.4 minutes.
- Motion heavy tests: 56 passed, zero failed. App heavy tests: 40 passed, one failed. Nine known-fail checks passed as expected.
- The failed pin is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` in `app:pocket3d_hsm`.
- The failure is the path count assertion at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`. Actual counts are `(3158, 3130, 1141)`.
- This platform uses the unmeasured macOS count range documented with #2371. Earlier safety assertions pass.
- Baseline check: remove all PR source changes in motion and app. Run the exact ignored heavy pin. It fails with the same counts.

title: perf(sim): share unchanged cut bricks between playback keyframes
body:
## What changed

- The three cut layers of `SdfField` (`cuts`, `cut_ups`, `cut_downs`) hold each brick in an `Arc` (`CutLayer`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field.rs`).
- A clone of the field copies the keys and the pointers only. It shares the bricks.
- A write goes through `layer_brick_mut` (`Arc::make_mut`). It copies a brick first when a clone still holds that brick.
- `claim_record` and `up_record` read the cell first. They take the writable brick only when the value changes. A move that changes no cell copies no brick.
- `KeyCost` has a new method, `key_bytes_after(prev)`. The keyframe store counts a keyframe by the bricks that the keyframe before it does not share, and by its map entries.
- `Keyframes::offer` and `Keyframes::held_bytes` use that count. The budget, the thinning and the stride law do not change.
- The public API of the sim crate only grows: `SdfField::cut_bytes_after` and `KeyCost::key_bytes_after` (with a default).

## Cause

A playback keyframe was a whole copy of the cut layers (#2181, PR #2192). Two keyframes one stride apart differ only in the bricks that the moves between them changed. The store paid for all bricks in each keyframe.

## Readings

Dense 100 mm face (`precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`, release, 4268 moves, 68 keyframes, stride 64):

| | Keyframe bytes | Calculation time |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream/main` (old sim sources) | 444 940 288 (424 MiB) | 49.8 s |
| This PR | 65 181 664 (62 MiB) | 30 s to 32 s (three runs) |

The factor is 6.8. The test asserts a factor of 6 at least.
The machine had other builds in progress, so the times are not exact.

Staged 24 mm face at 0.5 mm cells (debug, 28 keyframes): 9 923 808 bytes held. Whole copies cost 45 301 760 bytes. The factor is 4.56. The test asserts a factor of 4 at least.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` (`crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs`). It asserts the factor of 4, the equality of the running count and the audit, and the bit-identical replay at six positions.
- `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts the count on plain values, before and after a thinning.
- `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts that a clone is not written through, and that the cut over shared bricks is the plain cut, bit for bit.
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` (heavy lane, release). It now asserts the factor of 6 on the dense face.

Red before the fix: the first pin failed on unchanged code with `8454144 bytes held; whole copies cost 8454144`.

Mutations (each one red, then green after the restore):

- `offer` counts `value.key_bytes()` (the old line): `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` is red.
- `held_bytes` sums whole copies (the old line): the same test is red, `(5, 1, 40, 100)` against `(5, 1, 40, 40)`.
- `layer_brick_mut` writes through the shared pointer: `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` is red at "a shared brick is copied before the write".
- `claim_record` takes the writable slot before the read: `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` is red, `16358624 bytes held; whole copies cost 45301760`.
- All of `crates/sim/src` from `upstream/main`: `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` is red, `444940288 bytes held; whole copies cost 444940288`.

Unchanged and green: `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position`, `a_live_seek_after_a_cancel_keeps_the_byte_budget`, `the_worker_calculates_first_then_replays_and_the_post_gate_is_unchanged` (the replay is bit-identical, the budget holds, the post gate reads the same).

Gate on the final head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 11 steps, 0 failed (sim lib, `play_keys`, `play_precalc`, `stock_carry_side_exact`, `stock_columns`, `stock_field_cost`, `stock_sdf`; app `stock_field_cost`, `stock_play_precalc`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Heavy lanes that ran (release, `--ignored`): app `stock_play_precalc` and app `stock_field_cost`. The two are green.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` plans 217 steps for this diff. Only the two heavy binaries above ran. The other heavy lanes did not run. Run them before this PR is flagged ready.
- The `camcraft-ui` crate was not built. This PR changes no item that the UI crate can see, other than the two additions.
- The gate and the tests ran without sccache and with a target directory outside the worktree. The sccache daemon on this machine executed no compile, and a stuck `cargo check` of the editor tooling held the build lock of the worktree.
- `CostLedger` (the cut region, the full-brick ledger, the dirty set) is still copied whole by each keyframe. The store does not count it, as before.
- The time of one cell write was not measured alone. The dense face calculation as a whole is faster.

## Overlaps

PR #2714 changes other files in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/` and `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`. It changes none of the files of this PR.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2194-share-keyframe-bricks.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Simulation playback: keyframes share the stock bricks that no move changed, so the calculation before playback uses much less memory (the dense 100 mm face: 62 MiB, before 424 MiB) and keeps a shorter stride on large programs.

Fixes #2194

title: fix(sinker): judge body electrodes against cavity outlines
body:
Stacked on #2714 (merge #2714 first)

## What changed

This fix changes 23 files relative to parent `b95c27b2e`.
It adds `cavity_outline` to Sinker Burn parameters.
The points use coordinates relative to the burn point.
The project file, operation digest and MCP tools carry the outline.
An empty outline keeps the previous extent law.

The size law compares the electrode with inward cavity wall offsets.
It permits the derived diamond finish electrode.
It still refuses an oversized electrode by name.
It also refuses malformed outlines, contradictory dimensions and an incomplete finish.
Command creation checks the outline and its stated dimensions.
Generation repeats the bounds checks.
The existing scalar law keeps the floor and condition checks.

The MCP schema declares an optional array with a `null` default.
The electrode reply supplies an array for a body and `null` for a rectangle.
A `null` params patch clears the outline.
The independent stock verdict still checks the actual burn.

## UI screenshots

These inherited parent renders use the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU).
The before views show upstream `5ed5b7fe2`.
The after views come from parent PR #2714.
The pictured UI files are unchanged in #2836.
The images are stored only on `mkinney/Camcraft` branch `pr-screenshots`, at commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`:

|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |

## Cause

The previous law judged X and Y extents.
An inward offset moves a sharp diamond corner farther than the condition's undersize.

## Tests

Each mutation failed its pin with the old code or the guard removed.
Each pin passed after restoration:

- `old-generator`: red / green.
- `shape-point-limit`: red / green.
- `region-lattice`: red / green.
- `extentmatch`: red / green.
- `consumed-inset`: red / green.

Final targeted runs passed 11 app tests and 10 motion tests.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran 780 steps.
It passed 779 steps and found one failure in the rectangular MCP reply.

Each complete file diff was checked.

title: feat(ui): viewport Display menu with four display modes, Look at and graphics switches
body:
## What changed

- The viewport toolbar has a new button, "Display". It opens a menu above the toolbar.
- The menu has three groups:
  - **Display mode** (one choice): "Shaded, with edges", "Shaded", "Wireframe", "Shaded, with hidden edges".
  - **Look at**: "Look at a face". The next click on a face turns the view to face it.
  - **Graphics**: "Grid", "Origin axes", "Perspective view", "Orthographic view".
- Each entry has a tooltip. The active entries show a check mark (radio or check box).
- Each entry is view state. No entry queues a command.
- `draw_list::plan` gives the draw list of each display mode. `View3D::render_with` follows it.
- "Shaded" draws no wire on the model and on the stock.
- "Shaded, with hidden edges" draws the cached model edges a second time behind the faces, in a lighter tone. It builds no new buffer.
- The display mode and the grid switch are saved in the per-user `view.json`, with the gizmo names. An old file without the keys loads the defaults.
- The display mode choice moved out of the Browser pane ("Solids" radios). The Projection radios stay there.
- The wireframe button stays. One press gives wireframe from each mode.

Not in this PR: the quality preset, the ground shadow, the ambient occlusion, and "Look at" for a plane that is not a model face. Issue #2834 has them. #2818 permits this split.

The fourth mode of #2636 ("Wireframe, see-through") is not in this PR. #2636 stays open for it.

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for in #2818. The viewport had two display modes and no menu for them.

## Screenshots

Before (unchanged `main` at 380c29b3c):

| Browser "View" door with the "Solids" radios | Shaded | Wireframe |
|---|---|---|
| ![before view door](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/before-browser-view-door.png) | ![before shaded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/before-shaded.png) | ![before wireframe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/before-wireframe.png) |

After. The Display menu:

![after display menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/after-display-menu.png)

After. The four modes (the stock is hidden, so that the model shows):

| Shaded, with edges | Shaded |
|---|---|
| ![after shaded edges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/after-shaded-edges.png) | ![after shaded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/after-shaded.png) |

| Wireframe | Shaded, with hidden edges |
|---|---|
| ![after wireframe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/after-wireframe.png) | ![after hidden edges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/after-shaded-hidden-edges.png) |

The screenshots come from the off-screen harness of the guide images. They are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. No image is in this branch.

## Tests

Pins (all new, all green on the head):

- `ui::draw_list::tests` (6 tests): the draw list of each display mode, the traced stock, the empty document.
- `egui_app::tests::display_menu` (6 tests):

  - `each_display_mode_entry_sets_the_mode_and_shows_the_check`
  - `the_graphics_entries_set_their_fields`
  - `look_at_turns_the_view_to_face_the_clicked_face`
  - `look_at_on_empty_space_changes_nothing_and_says_so`
  - `the_display_mode_and_the_grid_are_kept_in_the_view_file`
- `egui_app::tests::page_layout_windows::layout_window_display_menu`: the layout test of the menu and its toolbar button.

- `display_mode::tests::each_mode_has_its_own_label_tooltip_and_key`
- `gpu_render::shaded_drops_the_wire_and_hidden_edges_add_the_far_wire` (a real GPU pass, it compiles the new shader stage).
- `view_file::the_display_mode_and_the_grid_round_trip_and_an_old_file_loads_the_defaults` (`camcraft-app`).

Red before the change: the pins use new types, so they do not compile on unchanged `main`. The mutation checks below show that each guard is pinned.

Mutation results (the guard was broken, the pin went red, the guard was restored, the pin went green):

| Broken guard | Red test |
|---|---|
| `plan`: "Shaded" draws the model edges | `shaded_draws_faces_and_no_edges` |

| `viewport_bar.rs`: the wireframe switch ignores the new modes | `display_button_toggles_the_menu_and_wire_works_from_each_mode` |
| `display_menu.rs`: a press on the button counts as "click elsewhere" | 5 `display_menu` tests, `layout_window_display_menu`, `click_toggles_view_state` |

Changed tests (the change explains each):

- `click_toggles_view_state` opens the Display menu for "Wireframe". The radio left the Browser pane.
- `view_names.rs` and `view_file.rs` build `ViewPrefs` with `..ViewPrefs::default()`. The structure has two new fields.

Gate on the head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (21 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The last commit after the gate changes one doc comment only; `cargo check -p camcraft-ui` passed on it.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` file, no `.cl` file and no snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run.
- The wasm build did not run. The menu and the render pass use only code that the two shells share.
- No frame time measurement on a large model. The hidden-edge mode adds one indexed line draw of the cached edge buffer.
- "Look at" on the machined stock mesh. The click uses the uncut stock triangle.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane). The toolbar is one button wider, so the cut must make the viewport goldens new.
- No person used the menu in the real window.

## Overlaps

- #2783 (`needs-rework`, `conflicts`) changes `viewport_bar.rs`: it adds tooltip text after `NAVS` and changes lines in `act` and `draw`. This PR adds `Nav::Display` to the same lists and one arm to `act` and `draw`. It touches the same functions on different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes, and #2783 then needs a tooltip for `Nav::Display`.
- #2786 changes `browser()` in `browser_pane.rs` at a different line (the Delete entry). Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2821, #2773, #2764, #2763, #2737, #2678 change `state.rs` or `egui_app/tests.rs` in other functions.

No new command, so no MCP tool is owed. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2818-viewport-display-menu.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: The viewport toolbar has a Display menu: four display modes (Shaded with edges, Shaded, Wireframe, Shaded with hidden edges), "Look at a face", and switches for the grid, the origin axes and the projection. The display mode is kept between sessions.

Fixes #2818

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket from the previous operations
body:
## What changed

The rest group of the 2D Pocket has a new mode, "previous operations".
In this mode the rest area is read from the stock that the earlier operations of the same setup leave.
The entered-tool mode of #1489 does not change, and it stays the default.

- `RestParams` has the field `source` (`RestSource::EnteredTool` or `RestSource::PreviousOperations`).
- `machining2d::rest_pocket_previous` plans the rest passes from a column grid.
  `rest_stock_from_columns` builds the `RestStock` of #2031 from that grid, one floor for each cut depth.
  `rest_plan_stock` makes the rest area from it.
- The grid is the one that `rest::prior_state` builds for the 3D Pocket: the setup stock, cut by the cached paths of the earlier operations, each with its tool shape.
- The reading is conservative:
  - A column stands at a cut depth when its top is above that depth. A floor allowance is material.
  - The standing columns grow by one cell diagonal.
  - A column that cannot be read stands. The pocket outside the grid stands.
  - The rest area is the union over all cut depths. A roughing pass that stops above the floor leaves the whole pocket.
- The two modes never use the planner of the other mode. Each planner refuses the other mode by name.
- The mode rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest.source` and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter.
  A file without the key reads as the entered tool.
- The Pocket page has the row "Rest stock from". The previous tool rows hide in the new mode.

Generation refuses by name when the stock cannot be established:

- an earlier operation of the setup has no toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup has a stale toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup is suppressed and has a cut on record;
- the Pocket is tilted (also refused at the edit).

The rest generator trusted the entered previous tool.
It could not see the depth that the earlier operation reached (#1490, item 3).

The rest path cuts each column that was left and cuts no wall.
- `crates/app/tests/rest_previous_ops.rs`: 7 tests. The real job against an independent simulation; the shallow roughing pass; the four refusals; stale after a changed tool, depth and order; `RegenerateAll`; undo and redo; the project file; MCP with save and reopen.

| earlier operation suppressed | same | red | green |

| earlier operation never generated | same | red | green |
| the Pocket arm routes the mode | `the_rest_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left` | red | green |

The first four guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off. The other eleven were removed by hand.

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

title: feat(2d): place typed text as single-line engraving strokes (InsertText, MCP insert_text)
body:
First slice of #2679. This PR does not close the issue.

## What changed

- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/` is new. It holds our own single-line engraving font and the layout of a typed string.
  - `glyphs.rs` is the glyph table: capital letters, digits, the space and `- _ . : / # + = ( )`. Each glyph is straight strokes on a 4 x 6 grid.
  - `mod.rs` has `strokes()` (polylines in mm) and `sketch()` (a `SketchData` on the layer `text`).
- `crates/app/src/commands/insert_text.rs` is new. `InsertText` is an undoable command. It places the typed text as a `Sketch` on the top face of the stock of a setup, at X, Y and an angle.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/sketch_tools.rs` has the new MCP tool `insert_text`. It calls `InsertText`.
- `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` lists the tool.
- `docs/decisions/2679-engrave-typed-text.md` records the decisions.

The text profile is the same entity as a DXF profile. `move_dxf_profile`, `DeleteEntity`, `get_job` and the project file work on it with no change. The project file format does not change.

## Cause

There was no way to make 2D geometry from typed text. A user had to draw the letters in a CAD program and import a DXF file.

Two facts of `main` set the scope of this slice:

1. The issue says to use a font from `assets/ui/fonts/`. The repository holds no font file. The outlines of the `egui` default fonts need a font parser as a new dependency. A new dependency waits for the maintainer. This PR uses our own stroke font, drawn from scratch. A single-line stroke is also the correct input for the centreline Engrave generator: it gives a solid mark, not a hollow letter.
2. On `main`, an operation on a profile refuses generation by name ("a toolpath from the chains of a DXF profile is not generated yet"). #1869 adds Engrave and Trace on sketch chains, and #1869 depends on #1864 (PR #2716). The toolpath, the verify and the golden CL of #2679 need #1869.

## Refusals by name

- An empty text.
- A character with no glyph. A lower-case letter is refused. It is not changed to a capital, because a silent change puts a wrong mark on a part.
- A cap height outside 0.5 mm to 1000 mm. A letter spacing outside 0 mm to 1000 mm. More than 256 characters.
- A placement that is not finite or is more than 1e6 mm from the stock origin.
- A setup that does not exist. A setup with no stock. A name in use or a reserved name.
- `stroke_text::sketch` fails if a stroke does not chain clean. A text profile cannot hold a rejected chain.

## Tests

Pins (red before the change: the test files did not compile, `unresolved import camcraft_geometry::stroke_text`):

- `crates/geometry/tests/stroke_text.rs`
  - `a_known_string_gives_its_golden_strokes` (golden strokes of `SN-0471`)
  - `each_glyph_chains_with_no_rejection_at_the_extreme_heights`
  - `the_whole_character_set_in_one_string_chains_clean`
  - `the_sketch_is_in_millimetres_on_one_layer_with_the_cap_height_stated`
  - `height_scales_and_letter_spacing_moves_only_the_later_glyphs`
  - `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`
- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/mod.rs`: `the_character_set_is_the_glyph_table`, `each_glyph_stays_in_its_box`
- `crates/app/tests/insert_text.rs`
  - `typed_text_lands_as_a_placed_profile_and_undoes`
  - `bad_text_and_bad_places_are_refused_by_name_and_nothing_lands`
  - `a_text_profile_saves_and_loads_with_its_strokes_and_place`
  - `the_mcp_tool_places_text_reports_it_and_takes_an_engrave_operation`

Mutations (each guard removed, the pin run, the guard restored):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `Y` drawn with three stroke ends at one corner | red: `each_glyph_chains_...`, `the_whole_character_set_...` ("3 curve ends meet ... a chain cannot branch") |
| Height check removed in `strokes()` | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Letter spacing check removed | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Length check removed | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Empty-text check removed in `strokes()` | green at first, so the pin was made stricter; then red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` (`Ok([])` in place of `Err(Empty)`) |
| No-stock check removed in `InsertText` | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...`, `the_mcp_tool_places_text_...` |
| Finite-placement check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |
| Placement range check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |
| Reserved-name check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |

With all guards restored, all pins are green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green. The change touches the shared crate `camcraft-geometry`, so the quick tier ran as the batch tier.

- Run 1: build, geometry (with `stroke_text`), kernel, cl, tools, post and sim suites: 227 steps ok. The worker tool stopped this run at its time limit in step 228 (`motion suites: lib`). It was not a test failure.
- Run 2 (`--only "motion suites" --only "app suites" --only "ui suites" --only "clippy"`): 709 steps, 0 failed, 53.4 min. `clippy -D warnings` with `--all-targets` on each crate is ok.
- After the gate, one doc comment in `crates/app/src/schema.rs` changed (it names `InsertText` as a writer of `Sketch`). Then `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the suites `insert_text`, `mcp_dxf` and `sketch_project` ran again: all ok.
- The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` and no `RUSTC_WRAPPER`. With sccache, each compile stopped with no progress on this machine.

### Heavy lanes on the reviewed head

Head: `c8734b4492a81a136b66845a2dc0c39626ce407c`.
Heavy diff-selection base: `upstream/main` at `495ef74789b06f9aeaab09a18dd08c9b8ef06a20`.
The tests ran on the unmerged PR head.

Command: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`.

The gate passed: exit 0, 217 steps, 0 failed steps, 27.5 minutes.
The release prebuild passed.

| Lane | Target steps | Tests passed | Expected failures (#1950) | Ignored |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Motion | 33 | 56 | 2 | 0 |
| App | 183 | 42 | 1 | 0 |

The dedicated checks confirmed the three expected failures. The gate counted those checks as OK.
These failures are separate from the tests that passed.

### Latest quick gate rerun

Head remains `c8734b4492a81a136b66845a2dc0c39626ce407c`.

Command: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`.

The quick diff-selection base was `upstream/main`. Its hash was not recorded separately.
The tests ran on the unmerged PR head.

The latest rerun finished with exit 1: 936 steps, 933 passed steps, 3 failed steps, 71.8 minutes.
All non-UI suites passed. The three failed steps have the same graphics limitations reported in the latest review:

- UI `lib`: 7 tests could not obtain a graphics adapter.
- UI `egui_app`: 3 tests returned exit code 1 instead of 0.
- UI `shell`: 1 test returned exit code 1 instead of 0.

The gate ran `clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` successfully for all eight crates.
This includes the touched crates `camcraft-geometry` and `camcraft-app`.

No source changed. The finding requested gate evidence only, so no new pin or mutation check was needed.
The earlier gate results above describe the original author run. This section records the latest rerun.

### Verification after the follow-up issue

The latest review requests one follow-up issue and a PR body update. #2891 records both missing items.
No source changed. The head remains `c8734b4492a81a136b66845a2dc0c39626ce407c`.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED, exit 1, 936 steps, 933 passed, 3 failed, 74.3 minutes.
- Base: `upstream/main` at `5fdbed9bd8e7a8bb28e6f162a02ab423842b77e8`. The tests ran on the unmerged PR head.
- The same 11 UI tests failed in `lib`, `egui_app`, and `shell`. The library reports no graphics adapter. All non-UI test suites passed.
- Gate clippy passed for all eight crates.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN, exit 0.
- `stroke_text`: 6 passed. `insert_text`: 4 passed. `mcp_dxf`: 2 passed. `sketch_project`: 14 passed.
- No new test or mutation applies to this GitHub metadata change. The issue labels and the PR links were checked through `gh`.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` file and no `.cl` file changes. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Not exercised

- No toolpath, no verify and no posted G-code from a text profile. Generation from profile chains is refused by name on `main` until #1869.
- No UI. There is no dialog and no viewport placement in this PR. The command and the MCP tool are the only doors.
- No script verb `cam.insertText`. Follow-up: #2891 (`MCP: InsertText`).
- Placement on a model face. A `Sketch` lies on the top face of the stock only.

## Open work for #2679 after this PR

- The Engrave toolpath, verify, post and golden CL on a text profile (needs #1869).
- The UI: type the text, pick the spot, set the height.
- The text as an editable parameter (needs a schema field and a project version step).
- Lower-case glyphs and an outline font source, if the maintainer wants them.
- The refusals for a text profile say "DXF profile". The wording is shared with DXF profiles and with PR #2716.
- #2891 (`MCP: InsertText`) tracks the script verb `cam.insertText` and the `insert_text` row in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`.

## Overlaps

- PR #2773 changes `ImportDxf::build` and `sketch::face_frame` / `sketch::stock_face`. This PR calls `sketch::face_frame` and does not change it. The files are different. After #2773 merges, `InsertText` can use `stock_face` for the named refusal of a stock with no flat top.
- PR #2716 changes `sketch_model.rs` and the operation code. This PR does not touch those files.
- PR #2678 adds lines to `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs` and `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` (different lines; the PR that merges second refreshes).
- The branch starts at `e048b103c`, and the gate ran on that base. `main` moved to `c4ac3ce6d` during the gate (#2149 and others merged). `git merge-tree upstream/main HEAD` gives no conflict.

Effort: high

Changelog: Typed text can be placed as single-line engraving strokes on the stock top (`InsertText`, MCP `insert_text`); the toolpath follows with Engrave on sketch chains (#1869).

Refs #2679

title: fix(gate): add the light tier for the heavy tests
body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate light` is a new gate tier. It runs the light twins of the heavy tests in release.
- The plan is one release build of the crates that hold a twin. Then it has one step for each test target with a twin (`motion light: lib`).
- A light twin is found from the source. Its ignore reason starts with `light lane:`. Its name is `<full test>_light`.
- The planner refuses a twin by name when its file has no `#[ignore]`d full test. A twin cannot take the place of its full test.
- The first twin is `the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/tests.rs`. It plans the slot 2 times. The full sweep keeps its 20 rows and does not change.
- A red light run prints a note for the PR. The note names each red step and the command of its full heavy step: `cargo xtask gate release --only "motion heavy: lib"`.
- AGENTS.md has two new named rules: **The light lane** ("Testing") and **Local full rerun** ("Commits and Releases").
- `docs/decisions/2569-light-heavy-tier.md` records the choices.
- The branch was refreshed against `upstream/main` at `744c0847b`. The merge keeps the upstream `heavy` tier and the new `light` tier.
- The tier pins now check both parser variants, both help lines, both error lists, and both rules in AGENTS.md.

## Cause

- A heavy test was skipped for each patch or run in full at the cut. There was no tier between the two.

Pins, all in `xtask/src/light_tests.rs`:

title: feat(ui): stock axis choice on the Stock page (along Z, X, Y or custom)
body:
## What changed

- The Stock page has a "Stock axis" choice: Along Z (default), Along X, Along Y and Custom. Custom shows three angles in degrees: turn about Z (yaw), tilt about Y (pitch), tilt about X (roll). The choice applies to a box and to a cylinder. The old "Rotation (yaw deg)" row is replaced.
- The turn is stored in the stock's existing `Location.rot`. There is no new shape field and no project-file version step.
- Apply sends the whole turn through the undoable `SetStock` (new UI queue entry `CommandKind::SetStockPose`; the old `CommandKind::SetStock { yaw_deg }` stays for its callers). Undo restores the old turn.
- The page reads a stored turn back. A preset turn shows its preset. Any other turn shows Custom with its angles (`camcraft_geometry::geometry::stock_axis`).
- Before any simulation, the page shows a plain note when the simulation cannot cut the drafted stock: a cylinder laid along X or Y, or a stock tilted off the axes. The note asks the simulation's own law (`stock_follow::sim_frame`). The refusals `OBLIQUE_STOCK` and `LAID_CYLINDER` do not change. A box laid along X or Y is a square turn, so the simulation cuts it and no note shows.
- MCP `set_stock` takes an optional `axis` ("z", "x", "y") or `angles_deg` ({yaw, pitch, roll}), not both. It calls the same `SetStock` and returns `{ stock, axis, angles_deg }`. The camcraft-mcp skill row is updated.
- `sketch.rs`: the DXF profile face ignored the stock's turn. Now an upright stock keeps its top face, a stock laid square is read as the same solid unturned, and a laid cylinder or a tilted stock is refused by name (`sketch::NO_TOP_FACE`). `ImportDxf` shows that refusal.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2576-stock-axis.md`.
- Follow-up: #2758 (stock simulation: cut a cylinder or box stock that lies along X or Y).

Process change: yes

## Readings

- X preset = a quarter turn about Y (stock Z goes to world +X). Y preset = a minus quarter turn about X (stock Z goes to world +Y).
- A laid 50 x 40 x 20 box at (3, 4, 5): the profile face is at the highest Z of the turned box, and its normal is world +Z (pinned).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/stock_axis.rs`:
  - `set_stock_lays_a_cylinder_along_x_and_undo_restores_the_old_turn`
  - `a_turned_stock_survives_the_project_file`
  - `mcp_set_stock_takes_an_axis_and_undo_walks_it_back`
  - `a_profile_lies_on_a_laid_box_and_a_laid_cylinder_is_refused`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_axis.rs`:
  - `the_stock_page_offers_the_stock_axis_and_custom_angles`
  - `apply_lays_the_stock_along_x_and_undo_stands_it_up_again`
  - `a_custom_turn_reads_back_with_its_angles`
  - `a_laid_cylinder_shows_the_simulation_note_and_a_laid_box_does_not`
- `layout_page_stock` now has the "Stock axis" anchor.
- `camcraft-geometry` unit tests: `each_preset_carries_the_stock_axis_onto_its_world_axis`, `custom_angles_read_back_and_a_bad_angle_is_refused`.
- The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by 4. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Gate

The gate is INCOMPLETE and is owed.

- Command: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head d067defa4. The quick gate fell back to batch, because the change touches `camcraft-geometry`.
- The coordinator stopped the gate at step 553 of about 900, to free disk space for an other gate. Steps 1 to 552 finished.
- 550 steps are ok. 2 steps failed:
  - `step_agreement` (`step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name`)
  - `feature_edge_g1_join` (`no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`)
- The two failures are those of the closed issue #2713. The branch base bbd28cccc is older than the fix in #2728. The trial merge with main in the review covers them.
- No other step failed.
- The pinning tests above pass. Clippy `-D warnings` on `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui` is clean.

## Screenshots

The pictures are renders of the real shell through the egui_kittest renderer (the same frame code), with the seeded test document and a 40 x 100 cylinder. They are not captures of a live app window.

Before (main):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2576/stock-before.png)

After, Along Z:

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2576/stock-after.png)

After, Along Y (the simulation note shows):

![after along Y](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2576/stock-after-along-y.png)

## Not exercised

- The live GUI viewport draw of a laid stock (the viewport already draws `Location.rot`; not changed here).
- A simulation of a laid box through the GUI (the sim law is unchanged and has its own tests).
- A DXF import through the GUI on a laid box (the command is pinned headless).

Changelog: The Stock page sets the stock axis (along Z, X or Y, or a custom turn) for a box or a cylinder, and says before a simulation when the simulation cannot cut that stock; MCP `set_stock` takes `axis` or `angles_deg` (#2576)

Effort: high

Fixes #2576

title: perf(motion): skip blocked doors in the adaptive routed return
body:
## What changed

The cause of #2736 is a slow path. It is not a loop that does not end.

- `adaptive::route::door` (in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/route.rs`) now refuses a door when the disc at the start point holds stock or wall. It refuses before it reads the leg law. Each leg capsule holds its start disc, so no leg longer than `ZERO_LEG` can pass there. The result is the same as before.
- The other door searches read the candidate cells nearest first and stop at the first legal leg. The old search read all free cells nearer than its best cell, in raster order. The chosen cell is the same: the nearest legal cell, and the lower index on a tie.
- `ZERO_LEG` is now one constant in `route.rs`. `lift_link::leg_ok` uses it.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/2736-adaptive-door-search.md`.

## Readings

These are on the issue's region (the box part, area offset 3, D6, optimal load 0.5).

| Build | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| release, HSM plan | 29.6 s | 9.8 s |
| debug, HSM plan | more than 9 min (issue) | 60.2 s |

- Before the fix, the microlift schedule took 23.7 s of the 29.6 s in release. In the schedule, 13 routed returns took 17 s. The door search took 16 s of that, over 53 routes. All 22 doors that failed had a blocked start disc. Each of them read the leg law on each free cell within 6 mm (grid 0.05 mm, about 58k cells).
- Output is identical by hash on nine cases (sizes 24, 18 and 12 mm by loads 0.5, 0.35 and 0.25). The load 0.5 case keeps hash `e3a88d5d82fabc7c` and 17680 moves. The nine cases took 201 s before and 103 s after, in release.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::adaptive::route::tests::a_door_on_stock_reads_no_leg`: a door from a point with stock in its disc gives None and reads the leg law 0 times. Before the fix it read the law 11289 times, and the test fails.
- `machining2d::adaptive::route::tests::the_door_is_the_nearest_legal_cell`: compares `door` with the old raster-order search on five points, with a mask on the free cells and a stricter leg law.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on head 3074ea19b: 8 steps, 0 failed, wall 7.7 min. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The app fixture after the fix, in debug and in release. Only the motion plan was timed after the fix.
- The tilted poses after the fix.
- The batch gate.
- The app plans the passes a second time when it carries the stock top. Follow-up: #2753.

Changelog: 2D Adaptive plans with routed microlift returns are faster (about 3x on a small pocket at optimal load 0.5); the posted output does not change.

Effort: high

Fixes #2736
